EUA querem data centers no país e taxam exterior
Na sexta-feira (20), o presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, declarou que não permitirá que empresas norte-americanas construam data centers fora do país. Segundo o republicano, as companhias que descumprirem a orientação terão de pagar um “imposto altíssimo“. A fala acende um alerta para o setor de tecnologia e para países que buscam atrair esses investimentos, como o Brasil.
A declaração ocorre em meio à disputa global pela infraestrutura de inteligência artificial. Na semana anterior, os EUA já haviam ampliado as restrições à exportação de chips avançados para a China e mais países, incluindo o Brasil. Agora, a pressão se volta diretamente contra a instalação de data centers em território estrangeiro.
Por que os EUA querem concentrar data centers
Um dos principais motivos para a tentativa de concentrar os investimentos nos EUA está no tamanho que os data centers passaram a ocupar na economia americana. Essas estruturas deixaram de ser apenas suporte para serviços digitais e se tornaram ativos estratégicos para a competitividade econômica dos países. Ao incentivar que os investimentos permaneçam nos Estados Unidos, Trump busca concentrar também os empregos, a arrecadação de impostos e os negócios relacionados à construção e à operação dessas infraestruturas.
Para o professor da FGV, a nova declaração de Trump revela uma preocupação norte-americana com a possibilidade de que investimentos em infraestrutura de inteligência artificial migrem para outros mercados. A fonte não detalhou o nome do professor, mas a análise indica que a medida é uma tentativa de reter capital e know-how dentro das fronteiras americanas.
O papel dos data centers na economia atual
Os data centers são a espinha dorsal da economia digital. Eles processam e armazenam dados que sustentam desde sistemas bancários até plataformas de comércio eletrônico e serviços de nuvem. Com o avanço da inteligência artificial, a demanda por capacidade computacional explodiu, tornando essas infraestruturas ainda mais críticas. Quem controla a infraestrutura de processamento tem uma posição estratégica na cadeia de desenvolvimento e utilização de inteligência artificial, destaca Alinie Mendes, cofundadora e CEO da Modular Data Centers.
Essa centralidade explica por que governos passaram a tratar data centers como questão de segurança nacional. A soberania tecnológica, ou seja, a capacidade de um país controlar sua própria infraestrutura digital, tornou-se um tema recorrente na geopolítica. A fala de Trump se insere nesse contexto de disputa por domínio tecnológico.
Limitações físicas e econômicas nos EUA
Apesar da pressão presidencial, a tentativa de concentrar os empreendimentos nos EUA pode esbarrar em limitações físicas e econômicas, além da eleitoral. Vivemos uma revolução tecnológica sem precedentes. A inteligência artificial, os serviços digitais, as redes sociais e o armazenamento de informações transformaram profundamente a nossa sociedade. Entretanto, por trás dessa modernidade existe uma estrutura gigantesca que poucos conhecem e cujos impactos ambientais ainda são pouco discutidos: os chamados data centers, ou centros de processamento de dados.
Essas instalações abrigam milhares de servidores que funcionam ininterruptamente, processando informações e sustentando boa parte do mundo digital. Embora não apresentem necessariamente chaminés lançando fumaça, possuem uma pegada ambiental significativa. É o que podemos chamar de poluição invisível da era digital.
E essa discussão chegou ao Espírito Santo. O município de Baixo Guandu, no Noroeste capixaba, poderá receber um empreendimento estimado em R$ 7,4 bilhões, com capacidade inicial prevista de 100 megawatts, destinado principalmente ao processamento de dados e à inteligência artificial. Trata-se de um investimento expressivo, capaz de movimentar a economia regional e inserir o Estado em um setor tecnológico estratégico.
Os benefícios são inegáveis. Durante a construção, a expectativa divulgada é de centenas de empregos, além da movimentação do comércio, da construção civil e dos serviços. Na operação, haverá oportunidades para profissionais especializados e possibilidades de aumento da arrecadação municipal. Entretanto, é importante lembrar que o número de empregos permanentes tende a ser muito menor que o registrado durante as obras.
Mas precisamos fazer uma pergunta fundamental: qual será o verdadeiro custo ambiental desse desenvolvimento?
Data centers exigem enormes quantidades de eletricidade para alimentar seus equipamentos e sistemas de refrigeração. Quando essa energia depende de fontes poluentes, aumentam as emissões de gases de efeito estufa. Mesmo quando utilizam fontes renováveis, continuam exigindo infraestrutura, investimentos e capacidade de fornecimento de energia.
Outro ponto preocupante é a água. Dependendo da tecnologia de refrigeração, essas instalações podem consumir grandes volumes desse recurso, principalmente por evaporação. Além do consumo direto, existe a água utilizada indiretamente na geração de eletricidade e na fabricação dos equipamentos.
No caso de Baixo Guandu, os responsáveis pelo projeto afirmam que pretendem utilizar um sistema fechado de refrigeração, com recirculação da água e perdas reduzidas. É uma proposta positiva, mas que precisa ser comprovada por estudos técnicos transparentes, considerando o consumo real, as necessidades de reposição e os impactos acumulados na região.
Não podemos esquecer que estamos falando da bacia do Rio Doce, marcada por uma das maiores tragédias ambientais do Brasil. A disponibilidade hídrica deve ser avaliada com responsabilidade, especialmente diante das mudanças climáticas, das estiagens e da necessidade de garantir água para abastecimento humano, agricultura e preserv

Impulsionada pela AI, a corrida por energia para data centers traz oportunidades ao País. Para Rodrigo Abreu, CEO da Omnia Data Centers, o País já possui “energia limpa, renovável, em abundância” para “um potencial grande exportador de energia na forma de valor agregado”. Abreu é o convidado de Adriano Pires no POWER, o videocast de energia do Brazil Journal.
Empresa do Pátria Investimentos, a Omnia desenvolve em Pecém (CE) um data center hyperscale com demanda elétrica total de aproximadamente 300 MW. A implantação gradual do projeto vai do 3º trimestre de 2027 até o início de 2029. “Levar os data centers para o Nordeste tem a vantagem de justamente depender menos das linhas de transmissão,” diz
Segundo o executivo, o diferencial brasileiro está na combinação de uma matriz elétrica quase 90% limpa com o Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN), que permite abastecer grandes consumidores a partir de diferentes fontes de geração. Segundo Abreu, essa condição reduz o risco de pressão sobre as tarifas residenciais, diferentemente do que ocorre em determinados mercados americanos. “A gente tem um grid completamente confiável, renovável e integrado,” diz.
Por fim, Rodrigo aponta bolsões com margem de capacidade elétrica para novos projetos. “São talvez os quatro grandes polos aqui: São Paulo, Fortaleza, Rio Grande do Sul e Rio de Janeiro,” diz.
O POWER é patrocinado por Copa Energia, Edge, Enel, Light, Ultra e Shell.
Também disponível no Spotify.

Melbourne Overtakes Sydney in Australia’s Data Center Pipeline
Melbourne now leads Australia’s data center pipeline, but power connections will determine how much capacity actually comes online.
Melbourne has overtaken Sydney in Australia’s data center development pipeline, with AI demand, power constraints, and planning conditions shifting new projects toward Victoria and regional markets. But most of that proposed capacity remains years away from operation.
Melbourne’s tracked capacity rose by 1.7 GW to 10.7 GW between the April and October editions of a report from DC Byte and Data Centres Australia, while Sydney’s fell by 3.6 GW to 7.8 GW.
Nationally, total tracked capacity – including operational facilities and projects at every stage of development – increased by 5.2 GW to 26.8 GW. But operational capacity rose by just 0.1 GW to 1.6 GW, underscoring the gap between large campus announcements and usable computing infrastructure.
DC Byte tracked 163 operational facilities and 97 proposed new projects, seven more than in April. Of those proposed projects, 52 have announced capacity above 100 MW. By comparison, only four operating facilities currently exceed that threshold.
Early-stage proposals accounted for 19.6 GW, or about 73% of the national total. Just 0.4 GW was under construction, a category DC Byte defines as data halls undergoing mechanical and electrical fit-out.
Teresa Tan, DC Byte’s lead analyst for Asia-Pacific, said the gap reflects the way projects enter the pipeline and progress through construction.
“A developer can add an entire campus to the pipeline in one update, but from an executional perspective, capacity comes online one data hall at a time,” she told Data Center Knowledge.
About 2.8 GW of the net increase came from early-stage capacity, where project sizes and schedules remain most susceptible to change.
“Some of that capacity will take years to deliver, while other proposals may never proceed,” Tan added.
Sydney’s Early-Stage Pipeline Shrinks
Sydney’s shrinking pipeline does not indicate a similar retreat in projects nearing delivery. Tan said the drop was driven largely by withdrawn or revised early-stage proposals, with growth in committed capacity partly offsetting it.
Early-stage capacity in Sydney fell from 8.6 GW to 4.2 GW, while committed capacity rose from 1.9 GW to 2.6 GW. Sydney still retained more operational capacity than Melbourne, at 0.9 GW versus 0.5 GW.
Matthew Lee, executive director and co-head of Australian data centers at JLL, said Sydney remains a priority for investors, developers, and customers despite ongoing power and planning constraints.
“Any shift in pipeline is not likely to be lost megawatts in my opinion, but there will be shifting timelines as individual projects are resolved,” he said.

artigo.texto: Emerging Alternatives to UPS in Data Centers Data centers are exploring BESS, rack batteries, buffer modules, and microgrids as UPS alternatives, with hybrid backup designs often the most practical path. For decades, uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems have been an essential component of most data centers. By providing short-term backup power and helping regulate voltage to servers and other IT equipment, UPS units have played a key role in maintaining uptime. But the power landscape is changing. A growing number of alternatives to traditional UPS devices are emerging, and many promise advantages such as longer runtimes, lower maintenance requirements, or better space efficiency. Here is a look at several emerging UPS alternatives, along with guidance on when it may make sense for data centers to move away from conventional UPS systems – or adopt a hybrid strategy that combines newer technologies with tried-and-true UPS infrastructure. Why Traditional UPS Strategies Are Under Pressure Before exploring specific alternatives, it is worth considering why UPS systems may no longer be the ideal answer for every data center’s power protection and backup needs. One major factor is the rise in data center power consumption. The more power a facility draws during normal operations, the more UPS capacity it needs to support critical loads during an outage. Because UPS systems can be expensive to deploy and often require battery replacements every 3 to 5 years, operators experiencing rapid power growth may be motivated to evaluate alternatives. The increasing use of on-site power generation is another driver. As more data centers add generation assets to supplement or reduce reliance on the grid, the preferred response to a power disruption may be an immediate transfer to on-site generation rather than depending solely on a centralized UPS to bridge the gap. Some new power protection architectures are designed specifically to support that model. Alternatives to Traditional UPS Systems Data center operators that decide conventional UPS systems are no longer the best fit have several options to consider. Battery Energy Storage Systems Extend Backup Duration Battery energy storage systems (BESS) use high-capacity batteries to store large amounts of electricity. Today, they are most commonly deployed to capture energy from renewable sources such as solar or wind for later use. But they can also play a role in data center backup power strategies. BESS and UPS systems both rely on stored battery power, but BESS systems are typically designed on a much larger scale. That distinction matters because a BESS deployment can provide backup power for much longer periods than a traditional UPS. While many UPS systems are designed to bridge only 10 to 15 minutes, BESS can support loads for hours, depending on system size and configuration. The tradeoff is cost. BESS generally requires a higher upfront investment and more complex integration. However, for data centers that experience longer outages, want to store renewable energy, or are building more flexible on-site energy strategies, BESS can be an attractive alternative or complement to UPS infrastructure. Rack-Level Batteries Save Space and Localize Protection Most data center UPS systems are centralized, supporting dozens or even hundreds of servers from a single installation. That model is relatively straightforward, but it also consumes valuable floor space that could otherwise be used to increase density and capacity. Rack-level batteries address that challenge by placing backup power directly inside the rack. In effect, they provide localized power protection without requiring the same dedicated floor footprint as a large, centralized UPS. They can also help reduce the heat concentration associated with larger battery rooms or UPS installations. Rack-level batteries share some of the same limitations as traditional UPS systems, including periodic replacement and lifecycle management. Still, they offer important space-saving advantages at a time when many operators are under pressure to maximize capacity within existing facilities. Buffer Modules Bridge Short Power Interruptions As their name implies, buffer modules are designed to absorb brief power interruptions or voltage fluctuations. If a server suddenly loses its primary power source, a buffer module can deliver enough energy to keep the equipment running while power is transferred to another source. Historically, buffer modules could bridge only milliseconds of downtime. Newer systems, however, can provide coverage for up to 20 seconds – long enough in some cases to support the startup of a diesel generator or another on-site generation source. That capacity is what makes buffer modules a possible alternative to traditional UPS deployments in certain environments. If the goal is to maintain server operation only long enough for on-site generation to come online, buffer modules may offer a lower-cost, low-maintenance option than a full UPS system. On-Site Microgrids Reshape Backup Power Planning Most data centers still rely primarily on the utility grid, using on-site generators only for backup or supplemental power. But some facilities are investing in on-site microgrids – collections of generation and energy assets capable of serving a substantial share of the facility’s power needs on an ongoing basis. In the right configuration, the microgrid can reduce dependence on traditional UPS architecture by improving resiliency and enabling faster transfer to local power sources. If sufficient generation capacity is available and the system is designed with appropriate redundancy, the facility may rely less on large, centralized UPS systems for extended backup coverage. That said, microgrids do not automatically eliminate the need for power conditioning or ride-through protection. As buscas na internet pelo termo “data center” aumentaram 170% no Estado de São Paulo nos últimos doze meses. Os números são do Google Trends, ferramenta que mede o volume de pesquisas.
O crescimento no interesse coincide com o início de projetos de grande porte, como um data center de R$ 3 bilhões autorizado em outubro para construção em Atibaia. A autorização para a infraestrutura foi concedida pelo Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS).
O presidente do Instituto Brasileiro de Proteção Ambiental (Proam), Carlos Bocuhy, aponta o espaço ocupado e a alta demanda por energia e água como os principais impactos ambientais desses centros de dados. “O funcionamento contínuo dos equipamentos exige refrigeração, processo que pode usar água e acabar gerando efluentes”, disse Bocuhy.
Além do consumo hídrico, a atividade gera outros problemas. A renovação constante de equipamentos produz lixo eletrônico, enquanto os geradores de emergência emitem poluentes. Vazamentos de combustível desses geradores podem ainda contaminar o solo e os recursos hídricos.
Bocuhy alertou que a captação de água por esses empreendimentos, especialmente em períodos de seca, pode comprometer o abastecimento público e prejudicar ecossistemas aquáticos. Segundo o Instituto de Estudos Ambientais e Energéticos dos Estados Unidos (Environmental and Energy Study Institute), um grande data center pode consumir até cinco milhões de galões de água por dia. Esse volume equivale ao usado por uma cidade com população entre 10 mil e 50 mil habitantes.
Os centros de dados também podem criar ilhas de calor e elevar as temperaturas ao redor, com impacto mais intenso em zonas rurais devido à remoção da vegetação. Outra preocupação é a poluição sonora. O ruído constante de ventiladores e equipamentos, além dos picos de barulho dos geradores, pode afetar o descanso em áreas tradicionalmente silenciosas.

Efeitos ambientais e soberania de dados: entenda impactos de data centers
Especialistas apontam impactos negativos, como poluição sonora e crise hídrica, mas ressaltam a importância de data centers para a soberania
São Paulo — No último ano, o interesse de busca pelo termo “data center” no Estado de SP cresceu em 170%, segundo o Google Trends. O aumento coincide com a expansão dos investimentos no setor e tem despertado a curiosidade dos paulistas — e também dúvidas sobre os efeitos ambientais desses empreendimentos.
Um exemplo está em Atibaia, interior de São Paulo. Em outubro de 2025, o Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS) autorizou a estrutura elétrica que permite a instalação de um data center com investimento inicial previsto de R$ 3 bilhões no município, viabilizando sua construção. O projeto ajuda a ilustrar por que o tema ganhou espaço no estado, apontado como um dos destinos de interesse para o setor.
O que é um data center
Um data center é uma instalação física que reúne vários computadores e equipamentos que executam serviços digitais e processam informações. Ele não é só um depósito de arquivos, mas onde os programas rodam e dados circulam entre usuários, empresas e a internet.
Quando você abre um vídeo ou faz uma transação bancária, seu celular não cuida de todo o processo sozinho. Ele envia uma solicitação pela rede. Um computador em um data center recebe o pedido, roda o programa, processa dados e devolve para você em uma fração de segundos.
Entre no canal de WhatsApp do Metrópoles SP
No interior de uma infraestrutura dessas podem estar servidores, sistema de armazenamento, equipamentos de rede (roteadores, switches e outros), energia de reserva (fontes de alimentação ininterrupta e geradores) e sistema de refrigeração. Para manter esses equipamentos funcionando, os data centers consomem grandes quantidade de recursos naturais, seja para geração de energia elétrica, seja para o fornecimento de água, importante para manter o resfriamento dos ambientes internos.
Impactos ambientais
Carlos Bocuhy, presidente do Instituto Brasileiro de Proteção Ambiental (Proam), explica que os principais impactos ambientais de um data center estão relacionados à ocupação espacial dos empreendimentos e às suas exigências energéticas e hídricas. Esses impactos começam já na construção dos empreendimentos, com a derrubada de vegetação nativa e a alteração da impermeabilização do solo, que pode levar à erosão e risco de assoreamento.
“Na operação, os servidores consomem eletricidade continuamente e geram calor, aumentando a necessidade de refrigeração. Conforme a tecnologia adotada, o resfriamento também pode consumir água e gerar efluentes, que precisam de tratamento e descarte adequados. Geradores a diesel ou gás, usados em testes e emergências, emitem poluentes; já a troca de equipamentos produz resíduos eletrônicos, e eventuais vazamentos de combustível podem contaminar o solo e a água”, diz Bocuhy.
Além disso, os data center podem gerar zonas

artigo.texto: CATL's China Battery Share Slips a Sixth Straight Month as Output Plans Meet a Storage Slowdown Published on 11/23/2026 at 07:32 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL's grip on its home battery market loosened again in October, with its share of batteries installed in Chinese vehicles falling to 40%, according to China Automotive Battery Innovation Alliance data reported by the South China Morning Post on Friday. It marked the sixth consecutive monthly decline for the world's largest battery maker, though the company still held the top spot in the rankings. The slide comes as the company's near-term manufacturing outlook draws fresh scrutiny. ZE Consulting's survey, cited by Citigroup in a November 18 research note, pointed to a cut in CATL's November 2026 production plan, attributed to softer demand for energy storage systems. The reduction applies solely to lithium iron phosphate cells, with planned output trimmed from 96 to 93 gigawatt-hours—about 3.1% below the original schedule—while ternary battery plans were left untouched. CATL has not confirmed the adjustment, and the survey tracks intended manufacturing rather than actual output. Citigroup Sees Possible December Follow-Through The US brokerage expects commercial-vehicle battery demand to partly offset the storage weakness, and flagged the risk of a further cut in December. Inventory destocking could stretch into the first quarter of 2027, in its view. A separate TD survey of 46 Chinese battery makers pointed to a 5% month-on-month decline in November 2026 production plans across the sector, though the precise figure for CATL remains an estimate. Those softer storage signals follow a stretch of robust shipment growth. SNE Research data show global energy-storage battery deliveries climbed 73% year on year between January and September 2026, with CATL topping the rankings on 198.3 gigawatt-hours and a 25.4% market share. The figures underline how deeply the company is embedded in the storage market, but they say nothing about whether November's planned volumes will actually be built. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Swap Network and Overseas Service Push Ahead Beyond the factory floor, CATL is pressing on with its battery-swapping buildout. The company aims to operate 6,000 passenger-car swap stations in China by 2027—5,000 in cities and 1,000 along highways—covering 297 cities. It had 2,520 stations across 200 Chinese cities at the end of September, by its own count. Leadership of that business is also shifting. Bloomberg reported on November 17 that Yang Jun, who oversees battery swapping, has additionally been handed the domestic passenger-car unit, along with a share of marketing responsibilities. He reports to chairman Robin Zeng. In Turkey, CATL opened its first NING SERVICE Experience Center in the country on November 19 alongside Ascendum Türkiye, combining battery repair with sales and service at the Istanbul site. The company also joined BYD, ACWA Power and Sungrow on November 13 at COP31 in Antalya to launch the Global Energy Storage Alliance, a grouping intended to promote large-scale storage deployment and international cooperation. No specific projects, investments or commercial agreements were fixed at the founding. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. For investors, December's production planning is the nearer signal of whether the weakness Citigroup described carries into the new year. artigo.texto: A instalação de uma fábrica de baterias da empresa chinesa Windey no Polo Industrial de Camaçari avançou mais uma etapa. A companhia foi cadastrada no Credenciamento de Fornecedores Informatizado (CFI) do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES), movimento que permite avançar no processo de habilitação de seus equipamentos para acessar linhas de financiamento do banco. O anúncio foi feito pelo Governo da Bahia nesta quinta-feira (19). O empreendimento prevê investimento de R$ 100 milhões e ocupará uma área de aproximadamente 25 mil metros quadrados. A unidade terá capacidade produtiva estimada em 2 gigawatt-hora (GWh) por ano, com previsão de começar a operar em 2027. Será a primeira fábrica de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias da Windey fora da China, com produção destinada aos mercados brasileiro e latino-americano. Apesar do avanço no cadastro, o equipamento VOLTPACK L5015, que será produzido pela empresa, ainda passa por análise do BNDES para obtenção do credenciamento específico. A habilitação é considerada estratégica diante das exigências de conteúdo nacional previstas em uma das modalidades do Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade de 2026, marcado para os dias 2 e 4 de dezembro. O projeto também representa uma oportunidade de geração de empregos em Camaçari. Em junho deste ano, durante o lançamento da pedra fundamental da fábrica, o presidente da Windey Brasil, Ricardo Galvão, estimou que a operação poderá contar com aproximadamente 70 a 120 profissionais quando estiver funcionando plenamente. A empresa também prevê parcerias com o SENAI CIMATEC e outras instituições para capacitação de trabalhadores em áreas técnicas e industriais. A Windey não estará sozinha na disputa por esse mercado. Entre as empresas que se movimentam para fornecer equipamentos de armazenamento de energia estão a pernambucana Moura, que anunciou investimento de R$ 200 milhões em Belo Jardim, e a chinesa CRRC, que negocia a implantação de uma unidade de montagem em Sergipe. Fabricantes como WEG, BYD e outras companhias também participam desse mercado em expansão. A tecnologia produzida pela Windey é considerada estratégica para o setor elétrico. Os sistemas de armazenamento em baterias permitem guardar a energia gerada em períodos de maior produção, principalmente pelas fontes solar e eólica, para utilizá-la quando a geração diminui ou a demanda aumenta. A solução contribui para reduzir oscilações no fornecimento e ampliar a capacidade de integração das fontes renováveis à rede elétrica. A chegada da empresa integra uma estratégia de expansão de sua presença na Bahia. Em 2025, a Windey inaugurou um escritório nacional e um Centro de Pesquisa e Desenvolvimento em Salvador, em parceria com o SENAI CIMATEC. Com a nova unidade industrial em Camaçari, o estado busca ampliar sua participação em um setor que reúne tecnologia, investimentos internacionais e oportunidades de desenvolvimento econômico. Fonte: Movimento Econômico, Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Econômico da Bahia e Governo do Estado.

artigo.texto: Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh to Share 500 MW Renewable Energy Storage Capacity Updated: Nov 21, 2026 01:02:28pm Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh to Share 500 MW Renewable Energy Storage Capacity New Delhi, Nov 21 (KNN) In a first-of-its-kind arrangement, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh will jointly use a 500 MW pumped storage capacity to meet peak-hour electricity demand. The arrangement is being described as India's first complementarity-based inter-state energy storage procurement. On Wednesday, Madhya Pradesh Power Management Company Limited (MPPMCL) and Uttar Pradesh selected the developers for the project through an e-reverse auction, as reported by Hindustan Times. Two States to Use Storage Capacity for Six Months Each Madhya Pradesh Energy Secretary Vishesh Gadpale said the two states have different periods of peak electricity demand. Madhya Pradesh requires more power between November and April due to the rabi crop season and winter demand, while Uttar Pradesh sees higher demand from May to October because of paddy cultivation and increased air-conditioning use during summer. “Instead of both states buying separate 500 MW power for entire year, we will use the same capacity for six months each,” Gadpale said. The project will store 500 MW of power for six hours and supply electricity continuously for four hours. It will be backed by a 40-year power purchase agreement. JSW Neo Energy Limited and Torrent Energy Storage Solutions Private Limited have won the bid, an official said. The project's location will be finalised after the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) approves the tariff under Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003. Each State to Pay Rs 674 Crore According to the official, each state will pay Rs 674 crore at a rate of Rs 1.3487 crore per MW per year. This includes the cost of electricity lost during the storage and discharge cycle. The official said the tariff is lower than rates offered in recent pumped storage project bids elsewhere in the country. Under conventional arrangements, states book and pay for storage capacity throughout the year but use it intensively for only six or seven months. “In our arrangement, the same 500 MW capacity will be utilised year-round, six months by Madhya Pradesh and six months by Uttar Pradesh. For the developer, there is no idle period,” the official said. Gadpale added that both states would share the fixed capacity cost. The project will store surplus solar energy generated during the day and release it during evening peak demand hours. Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Managing Director Nitesh Kumar said the arrangement would benefit both states by improving access to electricity during peak hours. “This collaboration is going to benefit both states equally. During peak hours, we need to purchase power from the exchange and we also do banking. Many times we faced problems due to unavailability of energy in the exchange. This collaboration will help both states. It is cost effective,” he said. (KNN Bureau)

artigo.texto: Trump ameaça taxar empresas que construírem data centers fora dos EUA Atualizado O presidente Donald Trump fez uma defesa enfática das políticas econômicas de seu governo, prometeu redobrar os esforços para construir centros de dados nos Estados Unidos e ameaçou impor impostos punitivos às empresas que os construírem no exterior durante uma coletiva de imprensa na Casa Branca nesta sexta-feira. — Vamos lutar muito pelos centros de dados — disse Trump, afirmando que não queria que a China assumisse a liderança no setor. — Estamos na frente e eles estão em segundo lugar. O presidente também destacou o que considera conquistas diplomáticas de sua viagem-relâmpago à Ásia nesta semana, que incluiu a primeira reunião trilateral da história com os líderes da Rússia e da China. Ele classificou a viagem como uma agenda "excelente e de grande importância" e promoveu alguns dos acordos comerciais que havia firmado, incluindo o entendimento com as Filipinas. A viagem, no entanto, não produziu planos concretos para enfrentar preocupações globais, como as guerras no Irã e na Ucrânia, os riscos da inteligência artificial ou a proliferação nuclear. Os comentários sobre a expansão dos centros de dados foram feitos semanas depois de eleitores de diferentes partes dos Estados Unidos aprovarem moratórias para interromper ou limitar a construção dessas instalações e manifestarem profundas preocupações com a inteligência artificial. Trump, no entanto, reiterou seu apoio inabalável ao que chamou de "superinteligência". Durante a viagem de quatro dias pela Ásia, Trump participou de cúpulas nas Filipinas e na China e se reuniu com o presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, e o líder chinês, Xi Jinping. A Casa Branca procurou apresentar a viagem como uma demonstração "histórica" do poder americano no cenário global, embora ela tenha produzido pouco além de oportunidades para fotos de Trump, que há muito demonstra afinidade tanto por Xi quanto por Putin, a quem chama de amigos. Trump voltou a um país em clima de tensão e diante de questionamentos sobre a capacidade de liderança de seu governo, após uma série de crises digitais, incluindo colapsos nos sistemas de aviação e interrupções nos serviços de grandes instituições bancárias. Durante a viagem, o presidente praticamente ignorou as preocupações internas, desde as falhas nos sistemas até a queda prolongada do mercado de ações. Confira os principais destaques da coletiva de imprensa: - Nvidia: Trump voltou a defender Jensen Huang, afastado do comando da Nvidia, argumentando que ele deveria pedir desculpas e ser reconduzido ao cargo de presidente-executivo. -- Temos que proteger nossas pessoas brilhantes. Jensen é uma delas -- disse Trump. - Putin: Trump voltou a afirmar que considera Putin um amigo, apesar de a Rússia ser aliada do Irã no conflito com os Estados Unidos. Questionado se considerava Putin um amigo da América, respondeu: — Não posso falar pela América. Em seguida, disse que Putin havia sido gentil com ele durante a investigação sobre uma possível interferência russa nas eleições de 2016. - Guerra na Ucrânia: Trump atribuiu a falta de avanços em um acordo de paz na Ucrânia, conflito que, há dois anos, afirmou que conseguiria encerrar rapidamente, ao "ódio imenso" entre os presidentes da Ucrânia e da Rússia. — Só posso dizer que o presidente Putin gostaria de resolver essa questão, e disso tenho certeza — afirmou. - Groenlândia: Um dia depois de a Dinamarca aprovar um novo acordo de segurança que reafirma a presença militar americana na Groenlândia, Trump declarou: — Nós temos a Groenlândia. Temos isso de forma muito sólida. O acordo basicamente reafirma um pacto de 1951 e está muito distante da ambição de Trump de adquirir a ilha do Ártico como território dos Estados Unidos. - Cooperação com os democratas: Questionado sobre a política interna após as expressivas derrotas dos republicanos nas eleições legislativas de meio de mandato, o presidente disse estar otimista quanto à possibilidade de trabalhar com os democratas, que em breve controlarão o Congresso. Ele afirmou que usaria seu poder de veto tanto para barrar projetos de lei quanto como instrumento de pressão nas negociações sobre temas como saúde. — Podemos acabar nos saindo melhor do que lidando com os republicanos — disse, ao descrever o deputado Hakeem Jeffries, de Nova York, e o senador Chuck Schumer, também de Nova York, como líderes inteligentes. - Chefe de segurança cibernética: Trump disse que demitiu Sean Cairncross, diretor nacional de segurança cibernética, "porque não achava que aquela pessoa fosse boa o suficiente". Ele não forneceu mais detalhes. Cairncross deixou o cargo após uma série de interrupções tecnológicas afetar empresas americanas e órgãos do governo federal.

artigo.texto: Malaysian developer Kerjaya Prospek Property Bhd has said one of its subsidiaries is buying 34 battery energy storage system (BESS) units in a deal worth about MYR 5.26 million. The units will go into Menara Vista Petaling, home to the developer’s Bloomsvale project on Old Klang Road in Kuala Lumpur. The order has been placed with a 70%-owned unit of ES Sunlogy Bhd, an engineering firm in which construction group Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd holds a 31% stake. It is the latest in a run of business deals between the Kerjaya companies and ES Sunlogy. Representative image Kerjaya Prospek Property Bhd (KPPROP), formerly known as GSB Group Bhd, has told Bursa Malaysia that one of its units is acquiring 34 battery energy storage system units. The purchase is valued at MYR 5.26 million. Advertisement The buyer is Kerjaya Property Sdn Bhd (KPSB). It placed the order with Sunlogy Asia Energy Storage Sdn Bhd (SAES), a 70%-owned subsidiary of ES Sunlogy Bhd, which accepted it on Tuesday. The order covers the supply, delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of the units at Menara Vista Petaling in Kuala Lumpur, at a fixed value of MYR 5,260,619. Menara Vista Petaling is the site of Bloomsvale, the developer’s mixed-use project. It sits on 5.2 acres of freehold land along Jalan Klang Lama (Old Klang Road). Its serviced residence tower has 66 floors and 1,199 units and was completed in 2023. The development also has retail and office space, which adds to the group’s recurring income. A BESS stores surplus electricity for later use. For a building, it helps keep energy costs steady, cushion grid disruptions and manage peak power demand. The order is a related-party deal. Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd holds a 31% equity interest in ES Sunlogy. ES Sunlogy said it had no other transactions with KPSB in the previous 12 months, so its total dealings with KPSB over that period equal the value of this order. Kerjaya Prospek Group chairman Datuk Seri Tee Eng Ho, along with members of his family, has interests in KPPROP. Kerjaya Prospek Group built its ES Sunlogy stake in quick steps. It first subscribed to 70 million new shares for MYR 18.76 million in July, taking a 9.09% stake. It then bought 19.18% for MYR 40.18 million and a further 2.73% for MYR 5.36 million, reaching 31%. In all, it invested about MYR 64.31 million. The chairman said the group intends to keep the stake at 31% for now, which is about two percentage points below the 33% level that would trigger a mandatory general offer. The two groups have worked together for years. ES Sunlogy shareholders approved a recurrent related-party transactions mandate last month to ease routine dealings with Kerjaya Prospek. Earlier this month, ES Sunlogy’s unit Savelite Engineering won two subcontracts worth a combined MYR 25.07 million from Kerjaya Prospek (M) Sdn Bhd for electrical and infrastructure works on Pulau Andaman in Penang. Savelite had also secured an electrical subcontract from Kerjaya Prospek (M) at the start of the year for a development by Pixel Valley Sdn Bhd, a KPPROP unit. Battery storage is a growing line for ES Sunlogy. The company has already put battery systems at construction sites in Singapore to cut the use of diesel generators. It plans to take part in the Large Scale Solar 6 (LSS6) programme as a developer, aiming for at least 100MW with a battery storage component. For KPPROP, the purchase comes as it lines up new projects. The developer has a serviced apartment pipeline with an estimated gross development value of about MYR 2 billion over the next one to two years, backed by a 60-acre landbank. The order is small in value, but it is one of the first times a Kerjaya company has bought battery storage from ES Sunlogy rather than only electrical works. How the 34 units perform in a busy mixed-use building could decide whether similar systems are fitted in the developer’s upcoming serviced apartments. Investors are also likely to keep an eye on the growing number of related-party deals between the companies, since Bursa rules require such transactions to be added together when judging their size. Malaysia’s Energy Commission has also set out safety guidelines for battery storage systems, which will apply to installations of this kind. artigo.texto: Enquanto o mundo discute o futuro dos combustíveis fósseis, a expansão da inteligência artificial cria um novo desafio ambiental. Um estudo mostra que os data centers nos Estados Unidos já emitem mais poluição do que alguns países. São 403 galpões. Os maiores centros de dados dos Estados Unidos. Juntos, eles colocam mais gás carbônico na atmosfera do que países como a Jordânia, a Guatemala e o Quênia. Quase a mesma quantidade que Bolívia e Dinamarca. É o que descobriram pesquisadores da Universidade de Harvard. "As emissões somaram 26 milhões de toneladas. Pense nisso: estamos falando de emissões de carbono comparáveis às de um país inteiro. Imagine toda a população, todas as indústrias, as casas, os hospitais", disse um pesquisador de Harvard. O estudo revela ainda que 54% da energia que alimenta esses data centers vêm de combustíveis fósseis, como gás natural e carvão. E não se trata de pouca energia: Quando você ou qualquer pessoa faz uma pergunta para a inteligência artificial, a informação vai direto para datacenters. Lá, milhares de computadores funcionam 24 horas por dia executando milhares e milhares de cálculos. Quanto mais os datacenters puxam energia pra funcionar, mais as usinas trabalham e mais gás carbônico é lançado na atmosfera. Isso tudo é necessário para que a resposta volte para os nossos computadores, em poucos segundos. Agora, imagine milhões de pessoas fazendo perguntas para a IA, várias e várias vezes. A Virginia é o estado americano com o maior numero de data centers. Por lá, as autoridades planejam construir uma torre de energia mais alta que a Estátua da Liberdade pra conseguir dar conta da demanda da região. Em 2025, para abastecer o mercado de inteligência artificial, o governo Trump adiou ou cancelou o fechamento da maior parte das usinas de carvão. O que está acontecendo nos Estados Unidos vai contra o maior acordo ambiental já feito nas últimas décadas. Em 2015, 193 países assinaram o Acordo de Paris. Uma das metas é diminuir a dependência de fontes de energia sujas, para conter o aquecimento global. Mas, em 2025, Trump repetiu o que já tinha feito no primeiro mandato e retirou os Estados Unidos do acordo. Para Gianluca Guidi, um dos responsáveis pela pesquisa em Harvard, é possível diminuir o abismo entre inteligência artificial e meio ambiente. No Orgeon alguns datacenters funcionam a partir de hidrelétricas. Empresas de tecnologia estudam a construção de centros de dados debaixo d'água, resfriados pelo mar a e movidos à energia limpa. "Existem formas de construir melhor, mas isso leva tempo. Então seria. Enquanto não houver regulamentação, algo que obrigue todo mundo a fazer a mesma coisa não existe incentivo. Construir debaixo d’água ou no espaço é muito caro, exige mais investimento e tempo. E numa corrida como essa, ninguém quer ficar para trás", afirmou Gianluca Guidi, um dos responsáveis pela pesquisa em Harvard. artigo.texto: India’s rapid renewable capacity addition, which continues to outpace transmission augmentation, particularly in resource-rich states such as Rajasthan and Gujarat, is increasing grid congestion and the need for storage to absorb surplus generation, shift supply to non-solar hours and ease network constraints. The country's battery energy storage system (BESS) market is moving from tendering to execution, backed by strong policy support and a large tender pipeline, ratings agency ICRA said in a report. "However, the rebound in battery prices, rupee depreciation and aggressive bids make timely battery procurement, robust long-term service agreements and offtake tie-ups critical for project viability," it said. According to the report, strong energy storage demand and a sizeable tender pipeline are supporting growth in the sector, but execution remains a key monitorable. "Operational BESS capacity is also rising, signalling progress from tendering to deployment. Policy support, including the government's Viability Gap Funding schemes announced in 2023, 2025 and 2026 covering 135.8 gigawatt-hours, provides a significant source of capital support," the report said. ICRA added that the viability of the recently aggressively bid projects would critically depend on battery procurement costs and currency movements. For developers in the renewable energy sector, costs not covered by the supplier, including performance penalties, additional batteries and post-warranty maintenance, are important risks. "At a battery pack cost of USD 70 per kilowatt-hour, the cumulative debt service coverage ratio of 1.17-1.27 times is expected at tariffs of Rs 2.60-2.80 lakh per megawatt per month. Competitive procurement and protection against cost escalation remain central to the assessment," the report said. It added that lower upfront funding and supplier guarantees do not eliminate future costs and operating risks, and project assessment should account for eventual duty payments and check whether supplier guarantees adequately cover commitments to the power buyer.

artigo.texto: Gasgoo Munich- On November 16, China Southern Power Grid ("CSG")and CATL signed a strategic cooperation framework agreement in Guangzhou, CSG announced via its official WeChat account. Qian Chaoyang, chairman and Party secretary of CSG, and Robin Zeng, chairman and CEO of CATL, jointly witnessed the signing. Liu Wei, member of the Party Leadership Team and vice president of CSG, and Wu Yingming, board member of CATL, signed the agreement on behalf of their respective organizations. Image Source: CATL Under the agreement, the two sides will collaborate on R&D, zero-carbon scenario development, energy storage ecosystems, industrial synergy, and international business — all aimed at advancing the construction of a new-type power system. Qian said he hopes the partners will jointly strengthen their edge in new-type energy storage scenarios, expand the open Power Hongmeng ecosystem, cultivate new growth in electricity-carbon synergistic industries, and broaden their international business footprint. Zeng, for his part, said CATL will deepen cooperation in technological innovation, joint platform development, and overseas business expansion to foster a healthy development ecosystem for the energy storage industry. The partnership comes amid a flurry of new energy storage policies. The 15th Five-Year Plan New-Type Energy Storage Implementation Plan, issued by the National Development and Reform Commission and the National Energy Administration, sets a target of 300 GW in national new-type energy storage capacity by 2030 — an order of magnitude increase from the end of the 14th Five-Year Plan period. The two parties had already established a collaborative foundation through the first phase of the Zhongshan Nanlang independent energy storage station, a 100MW/200MWh project powered by CATL's 314Ah lithium iron phosphate batteries and integrated with CSG Technology's self-developed energy management system.

artigo.texto: Com 700 MW instalados, país aposta em energia renovável e projetos bilionários, incluindo investimento de até US$ 39 bilhões no Ceará, para atrair gigantes da tecnologia TECNOLOGIA E INVESTIMENTOS Brasil concentra quase metade da capacidade de data centers da América Latina e mira expansão até 2030 Por Redação O Brasil se posiciona como um dos principais destinos para investimentos em data centers na América Latina, impulsionado pela expansão da inteligência artificial (IA), pela disponibilidade de energia renovável e pelo crescimento do mercado digital. Atualmente, o país reúne cerca de 700 megawatts (MW) de capacidade instalada, equivalente a quase metade da infraestrutura de processamento de dados da região, segundo levantamento apresentado pela revista britânica The Economist. A América Latina possui menos de 600 data centers, com capacidade conjunta estimada em 1,5 gigawatt (GW). Apesar da participação ainda limitada no mercado global, o setor apresenta perspectivas de expansão. O presidente da Elea Data Centers, Alessandro Lombardi, projeta que a capacidade brasileira poderá alcançar 5 GW até 2030, crescimento superior a sete vezes em relação ao patamar atual. Entre os investimentos previstos está a expansão da Ascenty em Vinhedo, no interior de São Paulo. A companhia planeja aplicar US$ 1,2 bilhão na região para ampliar sua infraestrutura e atender à demanda crescente por serviços de armazenamento e processamento de informações. O Ceará também ocupa posição estratégica nesse mercado. A ByteDance, controladora do TikTok, prevê investimentos de até US$ 39 bilhões em data centers no Complexo Industrial e Portuário do Pecém. A localização favorece a conexão com mercados internacionais por meio de cabos submarinos que ligam o Brasil à Europa, à África e a outras regiões. A matriz energética brasileira é outro diferencial competitivo. Aproximadamente 85% da eletricidade produzida no país tem origem em fontes renováveis, característica relevante para empreendimentos que exigem elevado consumo energético. Além disso, os custos de implantação na América Latina podem ser inferiores aos registrados em centros tecnológicos dos Estados Unidos. Levantamento da consultoria Turner & Townsend aponta que a construção de um data center no Vale do Silício custa aproximadamente US$ 14 por watt, enquanto os valores variam entre US$ 9, em Bogotá, e US$ 11,50, no México. O avanço da conectividade também estimula novos projetos. Com quase 80% da população latino-americana conectada à internet, a instalação de centros de processamento mais próximos dos usuários permite reduzir o tempo de resposta dos serviços digitais e melhorar o desempenho de plataformas e aplicações. Apesar das vantagens, a expansão do setor enfrenta desafios relacionados à infraestrutura elétrica, à segurança regulatória e às restrições internacionais sobre equipamentos avançados. Os Estados Unidos passaram a exigir licenças para o fornecimento de determinados semicondutores a data centers brasileiros, em meio à disputa tecnológica com a China. O governo federal busca ampliar a competitividade do país por meio de incentivos à instalação de novos empreendimentos e medidas para reduzir os custos de importação de equipamentos. A consolidação do Brasil como polo regional dependerá, no entanto, da capacidade de garantir fornecimento de energia, previsibilidade regulatória e condições adequadas para a execução dos investimentos.

artigo.texto: Hours after the University of Michigan’s Board of Regents voted to approve the University’s and Los Alamos National Laboratory’s planned data center, approximately 350 Ypsilanti Township residents, officials and experts gathered at Eastern Michigan University to oppose the project in a town hall meeting. Attendees condemned the planned data center — which is expected to stretch across 144 acres of the township — and its potential effects on energy costs, water and proximity to indigenous ancestral land. The panelists included Jay Coghlan, executive director of Nuclear Watch New Mexico, a nonprofit that monitors LANL; Michelle Martinez, director of the Tischman Center for Social Justice and the Environment; Ypsilanti Township attorney Doug Winters; Jamie Stuck, the state of Michigan tribal legislative liaison; and state Rep. Jimmy Wilson Jr., D-Ypsilanti. Attendees submitted about 250 written questions to the officials. Coghlan said he believes the choice of the project’s location comes down to one important resource for powering data centers: water. “Why is Los Alamos having the University of Michigan build a data center that’s going to use artificial intelligence to advance new-design nuclear weapons? Why in Ypsilanti?” Coghlan said. “My one-word answer is: water. … (Michigan’s) got water, and we don’t in New Mexico.” Next, Martinez said DTE Energy told shareholders this month it would spend $44 billion over five years to expand its infrastructure, partly to meet data center demand. She said that growth could strain water supplies in two ways: data centers use water on site, and then power plants that supply them, the largest withdrawers of water in Michigan, use even more. “You have this sort of weird trade-off situation with data centers and hyperscale data centers where it’s really difficult to measure,” Martinez said. “And there’s a lot of hydrologists who are increasingly interested in not only what’s being consumed on site, but also what’s being consumed by the power industry.” In response to a question about how to keep the University from buying more land in the township, Wilson Jr. said he plans to reintroduce legislation in January — which he predicts would have bipartisan support — that would require institutions to follow local planning rules when purchasing land outside their home community. The University has indicated that it plans to break ground on the center in late 2027, which it says will expand the University’s computing capabilities and research capacity. Winters argued the project does not serve an educational purpose. “This project is not a University educational purpose,” Winters said. “They have said from day one, this facility is 90% Los Alamos.” Winters then said the township has not set a date to file a legal challenge but does intend to wait until construction begins. “The township board has been very, very adamant that we will use every legal means necessary to stop this,” Winters said. Winters said the Michigan State Historical Preservation Office has advised the University to hire a federal archeologist and contact tribal preservation officers. He told the University the Ypsilanti community’s concerns should be held higher than the potential benefits the data center may provide the University. “You may have extraordinary financial resources,” Winters said. “You may have powerful friends in Lansing and Washington. … but you have come face to face with something your computers cannot calculate, and that is the heart of a community that refuses to be silent.” Ypsilanti Township resident Andy Melichar built a website that compiles residents’ public records requests about the project. He told The Daily he is not broadly opposed to data centers; however, he disagrees with the location of the University’s and Los Alamos’ data center. Experts have criticized the facility for its intended use in nuclear weapons research. “I’m not anti-data center,” Melichar said. “I just am not for putting them where we’re putting them, or for the particular purposes of Los Alamos having nuclear weapons in my backyard. I’m less than a mile away from where they’ll put this in.” Winters told The Daily he believes the project’s most pressing concern for residents is its tie to the federal government, as LANL’s core mission is to solve national security challenges through nuclear weapons design and performance. Michigan’s public universities, including the University, have constitutional autonomy that he believes is being misused in this case. “I think the worst and most pressing issue is the fact that Los Alamos and U-M, has sold its soul to the Department of War,” Winters said. “U-M is a Trojan horse, and they’re abusing their constitutional autonomy by saying, ‘Come on in behind us,’ when … the real dominant partner here is Los Alamos.” Daily News Contributor Eloise Nelson can be reached at eloisen@umich.edu.

artigo.texto: Gelion CEO on Worley partnership, battery scale-up and licensing opportunities Published: 04:50 23 Nov 2026 EST Gelion PLC (AIM:GELN, OTC:GELNF) CEO Matt Wood talked with Proactive about its pre-FEED collaboration with global engineering group Worley to advance production of its nano-encapsulated sulfur (NES) cathode material. Wood explained how Worley's expertise in cathode materials and sulfur processing will help Gelion validate manufacturing processes and develop preliminary designs for a potential pilot plant. The work will cover plant layouts, production requirements, cost estimates and project timelines, helping reduce investment risks ahead of a scale-up decision. Wood said existing production capacity can meet near-term demand, but additional volumes will be needed as commercial relationships develop. He outlined the company's strategy of expanding capacity in response to anticipated customer demand, rather than building ahead of the market. Finally, Wood discussed the potential to license NES technology, explaining how the Worley collaboration will help establish the manufacturing processes needed to support future commercial agreements and revenue opportunities. artigo.texto: ORANGE COUNTY, Fla. – The east side of Orange County doesn’t have a skyline. It has smokestacks. The Stanton Energy Center, run by the Orlando Utilities Commission, sits a few miles from the restaurants and homes of Avalon Park. It burns natural gas and coal, and it has solar panels on site. Most people nearby say they rarely think about it. Recommended Videos “From zero to 10?” Avalon Park resident Manouchka said when asked how often she thinks about the plant. “Minus five. It does not register.” But what happens at Stanton is changing, and not in the direction OUC had previously planned. OUC initially planned to put one of Stanton’s two coal-fired units into an extended shutdown at the end of May 2026, part of the utility’s long-running move away from coal. Then the federal government stepped in. On June 4, U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright signed an emergency order requiring OUC to keep that coal unit, known as Stanton Unit 1, available to run. The Department of Energy later extended the order through Nov. 30. Click here to see the order. “The Department of Energy said, hey, let’s pump the brakes on this and ensure that we have enough capacity to meet our current needs,” said Orlando Alancastro, OUC’s vice president of transmission. The emergency order points to the growth of data centers. It says that in Florida, “projections for resource and transmission growth lag behind what is needed to support new data centers and other large loads.” “As of April 2026, eight data centers are planned for construction in Florida,” the order says. OUC’s CEO, Clint Bullock, raised the same concern at a public workshop earlier this month. “The size of these hyperscalers is like nothing we’ve ever seen. You can’t forecast it into your traditional forecasting. That’s why this is a concern,” Bullock said. Hyperscalers are the massive data centers run by companies such as Google and Amazon. OUC says data centers are only part of the picture. The utility points to faster-than-expected growth in electric vehicles, more manufacturing, and a lack of new power generation across Florida. “There hasn’t been a whole lot of new generation that has been built in the last several years,” Alancastro said. Recent winter and summer weather events have also increased peak energy demand. As a result, OUC is increasing its reserve margin from 15% to 20% to help ensure reliable service during periods of high demand. At the workshop, OUC proposed its Electric Integrated Resource Plan, a 20-year roadmap, which does not take coal off the table. The workshop presentation is posted on OUCFuturePlanning.com. Under the plan, Stanton Unit 1 comes back online in 2028, converted so it can run on either coal or natural gas. Stanton Unit 2 gets the same conversion in 2029. The plan does not set an end date for burning coal at Stanton. “It leverages existing infrastructure. The cost to convert those units are far more economical than building a new resource,” Alancastro said. The plan also adds 150 megawatts of solar and 100 megawatts of battery storage by 2035. A gas plant with carbon capture and 345 megawatts of nuclear power are penciled in for the 2040s. Castro described those as placeholders that could change as technology develops. OUC says the plan still meets its goals of cutting carbon emissions 50% by 2030 and 75% by 2040, compared with 2005 levels. Coal’s share has already shrunk. According to OUC, coal made up 41% of its generating capacity in 2019 and 27% in 2025. Solar grew from less than 1% to 11% over the same period. What it means for your bill OUC says the plan would raise bills by about 1% a year for the next 5 years. There is some short-term relief. OUC is proposing a fuel charge cut that would lower a typical residential bill, based on 1,000 kilowatt-hours a month, by about $5 starting in April 2027. Avalon Park resident Jenna Egensteiner said she supports cleaner energy but wants the details. “Cleaner energy is obviously where you want to go. It’s just how, when, how much, for what,” she said. How to weigh in OUC is taking public comments on the plan through Dec. 4 at oucfutureplanning.com. The OUC board is scheduled to vote on the plan and the proposed fuel cut on Dec. 15.

artigo.texto: Ola Electric is betting that manufacturing its own battery cells can give it a lasting cost advantage in India's electric two-wheeler market. The company has commissioned 6 GWh of cell manufacturing capacity at its Gigafactory and is now working to improve production yields before integrating these cells into its vehicles. If the ramp-up succeeds, the investment could reduce its dependence on external suppliers, lower battery costs and improve the economics of its automotive business. However, the benefits will depend on how quickly production becomes efficient and whether the company can utilise the capacity at scale. With a market capitalization of Rs. 16,285.70 crore, the shares of Ola Electric Mobility Ltd were trading at Rs. 32.58 per share, down 0.94 percent from its previous closing price of Rs. 32.89 apiece. The 6 GWh Gigafactory moves Ola closer to battery integration Ola Electric has commissioned 6 GWh of cell manufacturing capacity, with commercial operations beginning in September 2026. This is an important step in its strategy to bring more of the electric vehicle supply chain in-house. Battery cells are among the most important cost components of an electric vehicle. Manufacturing them internally could give Ola greater control over procurement, product design and supply availability. It may also reduce its exposure to external suppliers as production volumes increase. However, commissioning capacity does not automatically translate into lower costs. The facility must achieve stable yields, consistent quality and sufficient utilisation before it can deliver meaningful savings. The cell business also remains small relative to the automotive business, with Q2 FY27 revenue of just Rs.3 crore and an adjusted operating EBITDA loss of Rs.38 crore. Cell yields will determine whether manufacturing becomes economical The biggest near-term challenge is improving manufacturing efficiency. Ola currently reports NMC cell yields of around 70–75%, meaning a portion of production does not meet the required quality standards. Management is targeting yields of 80–85% by the end of Q3 FY27 and approximately 90% by Q4 FY27. These targets are important because higher yields allow more usable cells to be produced from the same quantity of raw materials, improving manufacturing economics. Management expects that at around 70% yield, producing cells internally can reach cost parity with buying them externally. At 85% yield, it expects a 10–15% saving at the cell gross-margin level compared with external procurement. However, this is not the same as a 10–15% improvement in the automotive segment's overall margins. The benefit must first offset manufacturing expenses and translate into lower battery costs for the vehicle business. Until yields improve and production stabilises, the expected savings remain a management target rather than an established advantage. Captive demand could provide the initial scale Ola's automotive business is expected to be the first major customer for its cell manufacturing facility. Management estimates that the vehicle business could consume around 2–3 GWh of cells in FY28. Based on management's assumption of an average 5 kWh battery per vehicle, this requirement would correspond to approximately 4–5 lakh vehicles. This level of captive demand could help the cell business achieve an important utilisation threshold. Management expects the cell business's fixed and operating costs to break even against the economics of purchasing cells externally at consumption of around 2–3 GWh. This makes automotive volumes important not only for revenue growth but also for the economics of the Gigafactory. However, the company must first demonstrate that it can consistently manufacture enough usable cells while maintaining quality. If vehicle demand or production falls short of expectations, lower utilisation could delay the benefits of vertical integration. LFP cells and Gen 4 could further reduce vehicle costs Ola is also preparing to introduce lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells alongside its existing nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) technology. Management expects LFP production to ramp up during Q2/Q3 FY27, with yields reaching around 70% by Q4 FY27 and approximately 90% by Q1 FY28. From Q4 FY27 onwards, the company plans to integrate its own LFP cells into vehicles, with a targeted product mix of approximately 30% NMC and 70% LFP. The company also expects its Gen 4 platform, planned from Q4 FY27, to support further reductions in the bill of materials. These changes could improve vehicle cost competitiveness, particularly if Ola can combine lower cell costs with its existing engineering and component-integration capabilities. Management claims that its current bill of materials is already 15–20% lower than competitors despite offering higher functionality and specifications. This is a company claim and has not been independently established in the disclosed figures. The actual benefit will depend on whether the new platform and battery mix deliver savings without compromising performance, reliability or customer demand. External demand could support a larger Gigafactory Ola's longer-term ambition extends beyond supplying its own vehicles. Management is exploring opportunities to sell cells to external original equipment manufacturers and use additional capacity for energy-storage products under its Shakti business. The company has indicated that it could eventually expand the facility from 6 GWh to 20 GWh. Management estimates that capital expenditure per GWh could be below Rs.400 crore at a fully utilised 20 GWh facility, partly because the existing infrastructure has been designed to accommodate expansion. However, this expansion is not immediate. Management has prioritised stabilising the existing 6 GWh capacity before committing to a larger facility. artigo.texto: LAS VEGAS, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- WattCycle successfully concluded its participation in RE+ 2026, held November 17-19 at the Las Vegas Convention Center. At Booth C6820 in the Central Hall, the company presented its LiFePO4 battery, inverter and energy storage solutions and met with industry professionals, customers and prospective business partners from across the clean energy sector. For WattCycle, the show was a full three days of introductions, technical conversations and market listening, and it added another step to the brand's effort to grow its presence in North America. A Working Platform for the Clean Energy Industry RE+ is North America's largest clean energy event, bringing together companies active in solar, energy storage, hydrogen, microgrids, EV charging infrastructure and wind power. WattCycle took part to be seen and heard within that wider industry, not only within the battery category. The booth was arranged around three main product display zones, giving visitors a clear route through the range and a natural starting point for conversation with the team. Product Displays Organized Around Real Energy Needs WattCycle built its display around the situations in which people rely on stored energy. LiFePO4 battery solutions for recreational vehicles, marine systems and off-grid power stood alongside home energy storage systems and inverters designed for North American households, showing visitors how batteries and inverters work together as one system. Recent introductions, including an AI-enabled RV battery and two 32kWh home energy storage systems, were part of the display. The exhibition gave visitors a chance to explore the product range, understand its key features and learn how each solution can support a different energy need, from a camper on the road to a boat on the water to a home preparing for the next outage. Face-to-Face Exchanges on the Show Floor Throughout the exhibition, the WattCycle team welcomed 4000+ visitors to Booth C6820 and took part in discussions about battery technologies, energy storage applications and the changing needs of the clean energy market. Team members walked visitors through product features and application setups, answered technical questions and listened to how people in different markets use and plan for stored energy. Visitors who followed the booth's Energy Discovery Journey moved through each display zone with the team on hand to explain what they were seeing. These conversations were as useful to WattCycle as they were to visitors. They gave the team a firsthand view of what customers and installers are looking for, and a chance to exchange industry insights with people working across the sector. Launch Sessions at the Booth WattCycle also used the booth as a stage for two launch sessions held on consecutive afternoons. The first, on November 17 under the theme POWER WITHOUT LIMITS , centered on home energy storage and on making large-capacity systems simpler to install and easier to live with. The second, on November 18 under the theme FUTURE ENERGY, turned to the role of AI in battery management , with the AI-enabled RV battery at its center. Each session ran about half an hour and gave visitors an early look at where WattCycle's product development is heading, and the conversation continued with the team at the booth afterward. Interactive Moments Along the Way Alongside the product conversations, the booth offered lighter ways for visitors to engage with the brand. During the daily Power Hour lucky draw on November 17 and 18, visitors took a photo with a WattCycle prop and registered to enter. Others checked in at the booth for a photo and left with a WattCycle tote bag and an instant print, and visitors who shared photos or videos of the booth on social media and tagged @WattCycle received a branded cup or towel. Content creators were also invited to film at the booth and share their videos. These moments kept the atmosphere relaxed and gave visitors another reason to stay, look around and talk with the team. Early Steps Toward New Business Relationships Among those who stopped by were distributors, installers and other prospective business partners. Meetings at the booth opened discussions about possible cooperation, and WattCycle's business team will continue those conversations after the show. Companies interested in the partner program the brand introduced ahead of RE+ can follow up with the team directly. WattCycle sees these early contacts as the groundwork for future projects, not as finished agreements. The value of the week, in the company's view, lies in the relationships that can now be built on. What WattCycle Said About the Show "RE+ put us in the same room with installers, distributors and customers who told us plainly what they need from an energy storage system," said Steve, Chief Marketing Officer at WattCycle. "Those conversations help us shape our products and our support for the North American market. Ele afirmou ter se reunido com “pessoas incríveis” e ser amigo de várias, mas também falou em “inimigos”. A visita ao continente ficou marcada pelo encontro histórico com os líderes Vladimir Putin, da Rússia, e Xi Jinping, da China, em meio à cúpula da APEC (Cooperação Econômica Ásia-Pacífico). Trump disse que o evento teria deixado claro o “respeito muito impressionante” que todos na região têm por Washington. “Eu acho até que eles nos amam, mas eu prefiro que eles nos respeitem acima do amor”, afirmou. Among the innovations presented at Metstrade 2026 in Amsterdam, we saw a product that aims to revolutionize the world of marine propulsion. It is the Svenner II from EPT Technologies, the first solid-state marine battery to receive DNV certification. A solution that combines four features of particular interest to boaters: certification, high fire safety, long service life, and constant monitoring. The Svenner II battery from EPT Technologies The first thing that sets the Svenner II apart is its DNV certification, a major milestone for the marine battery industry. This certification confirms the battery’s compliance with rigorous safety and reliability requirements and offers benefits not only to shipyards and system integrators—who can rely on a pre-certified system—but also to boat owners seeking reliable solutions for onboard electrification. The battery is designed for use on various types of vessels, including both sailboats and motorboats. Greater Fire Safety The second advantage concerns one of the most sensitive issues when it comes to onboard batteries: the risk of fire. Svenner II uses solid-state technology that replaces most of the liquid electrolytes in traditional batteries with solid materials. This approach increases the thermal stability of the cells and significantly reduces the risk of uncontrolled reactions. The cells have passed particularly rigorous tests, including multiple overload and puncture tests, without generating heat or triggering thermal runaway. Furthermore, in the event of an accident, the DNV-certified solution allows the incident to be contained within a single module, limiting the impact on the rest of the battery pack. Over 10,000 life cycles The third key strength is longevity. Svenner II claims a service life of over 10,000 cycles, based on a depth of discharge (DoD) of 80%. By comparison, traditional lithium batteries average around 4,000–5,000 cycles. This means you can count on more than double the operational lifespan, with fewer replacements over the years and the potential to reduce overall operating costs. Integrated sensors and continuous monitoring The fourth advantage is monitoring of operating conditions. Svenner II integrates a system The BMS features a dual-core CPU in a lockstep configuration, which ensures redundancy and continuous operational monitoring. The battery pack also includes sensors to detect any water ingress and HVIL interlocks, designed to enhance module protection and monitor safety conditions. The system is also designed to operate in high-temperature environments, an important feature in the most demanding marine installations. artigo.texto: Mercado global de compostos de borracha butílica (IIR): Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de compostos de borracha butílica (IIR) até 2035, impulsionada pela demanda de embalagens farmacêuticas e armazenamento de energia Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de compostos de borracha butílica (IIR), o mercado chega a 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de compostos de borracha butílica (IIR) entra em uma fase de expansão constante, com a demanda projetada para crescer a uma taxa anual composta de 4–6% entre 2026 e 2035. Esse crescimento se apoia nas propriedades singulares de baixa permeabilidade e amortecimento da borracha de isobutileno-isopreno, que a tornam indispensável para vedações de recipientes farmacêuticos, revestimentos internos de pneus e um conjunto cada vez maior de aplicações de armazenamento de energia. As formulações de alta pureza e de especialidade, que representam uma parcela estimada de 25–35% do consumo global em volume, alcançam prêmios de preço de 30–50% e vêm redesenhando os polos de valor ao longo da cadeia de suprimentos. A oferta permanece concentrada em menos de dez produtores globais, com excesso de capacidade nos graus padrão convivendo com a disponibilidade restrita de compostos certificados para uso farmacêutico. A harmonização regulatória em torno da ISO 15378 e da ICH Q7 eleva as barreiras de conformidade e, na prática, consolida a base de fornecedores certificados. Ao mesmo tempo, a Ásia-Pacífico desponta como o centro de demanda de crescimento mais rápido, sustentado pela fabricação farmacêutica por contrato e pela produção de separadores de baterias. Este relatório oferece uma visão baseada em dados sobre tamanho de mercado, segmentação, fluxos comerciais, lógica de precificação e posicionamento competitivo até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado mundial de compostos de borracha butílica (IIR) projeta uma taxa de crescimento anual composta de 4–6% entre 2026 e 2035, com o índice de mercado subindo de 100 em 2025 para cerca de 155 em 2035. Espera-se que o crescimento seja desigual entre os segmentos: os compostos de IIR de grau padrão enfrentam pressão sobre as margens decorrente da volatilidade das matérias-primas e do excesso de capacidade, enquanto as formulações de alta pureza e de especialidade tendem a se expandir acima da média à medida que os clientes dos setores farmacêutico e de armazenamento de energia ampliam suas operações. A concentração da oferta em um pequeno grupo de produtores globais continua sendo uma característica estrutural, e é provável que os acréscimos de capacidade para material certificado de grau farmacêutico fiquem aquém da demanda, sustentando os prêmios de preço. Espera-se que os fluxos comerciais se desloquem para a Ásia-Pacífico, onde a fabricação por contrato e a produção de separadores de baterias avançam rapidamente. Entre os riscos de baixa estão oscilações superiores a 20% em um ano nos preços das matérias-primas petroquímicas e ciclos prolongados de qualificação de fornecedores, de 12 a 24 meses, que limitam a flexibilidade dos compradores. O potencial de alta reside na adoção mais rápida de compostos de IIR em formatos emergentes de armazenamento de energia e na contínua substituição, induzida por exigências regulatórias, por graus certificados de alta pureza. Vetores e restrições da demanda Principais vetores de demanda - Demanda sustentada por elastômeros de baixa permeabilidade em vedações e fechamentos de recipientes farmacêuticos, apoiada pela harmonização regulatória em torno da ISO 15378 e da ICH Q7. - Aplicações emergentes de armazenamento de energia, incluindo a produção de separadores de baterias, que exigem compostos de IIR de alta pureza com perfis rigorosos de extraíveis e lixiviáveis. - Crescimento da demanda por revestimentos internos de pneus, sobretudo na Ásia-Pacífico, onde a produção de veículos e os gastos em infraestrutura seguem robustos. - Migração para masterbatches de IIR pré-compostos e específicos para cada cliente, que encurtam os ciclos de qualificação e ampliam a captura de valor pelos formuladores. - Exigências crescentes de conformidade para graus de alta pureza, que consolidam a base de fornecimento certificada e sustentam preços premium. - Expansão da fabricação farmacêutica por contrato na Ásia-Pacífico, impulsionando o crescimento do consumo regional. Possíveis restrições ao crescimento - Volatilidade dos custos de matérias-primas, especialmente do isobutileno derivado de correntes petroquímicas de C4, com oscilações de preço à vista superiores a 20% em um ano. - Ciclos longos de qualificação de fornecedores, de 12 a 24 meses, para compostos de IIR de grau farmacêutico, o que limita a flexibilidade dos compradores e retarda a adoção. - Excesso de capacidade nos graus padrão, que comprime as margens dos compostos e desestimula investimentos em nova capacidade. - Gargalos de capacidade para IIR de alta pureza, já que as linhas existentes, originalmente projetadas para borracha butílica de grau para pneus, exigem investimentos significativos em acabamento em sala limpa e sistemas de qualidade validados.
