artigo.texto: American Battery Technology has seen its share price slide sharply in recent years, which naturally pushes investors to ask whether the current valuation is still supported by the company’s sales. With the stock now trading at around US$0.79, the key issue is how that market value lines up with what the business is actually generating in revenue. Over the past 5 years the share price has fallen 95.9%, which puts intense focus on whether the revenue base can justify even today’s much lower level. The business model depends on turning battery materials technology into consistent commercial sales, so investors are watching how quickly those projects can translate into stable top line revenue and cash generation. The issue now is whether the stock’s current price is well supported by American Battery Technology’s sales when measured against the Fair Ratio benchmark. Has American Battery Technology Run Too Far on Sales? P/S is usually the cleaner yardstick for a company like American Battery Technology that is still reporting losses, because it compares the share price with the revenue it already books rather than profits that are not yet there. On this measure, American Battery Technology trades on a P/S of about 5.0x, which is almost identical to the peer group near 5.0x and more than double the wider metals and mining sector at roughly 2.2x. The Fair Ratio model, which blends factors such as the firm’s growth profile, margins, size and risk, flags that this current multiple screens as overvalued and suggests the penalty for ongoing losses and execution risk is steep. The gap is so wide that the Fair Ratio output is better read as a warning sign that the stock prices its revenue stream very expensively on this framework, rather than a precise fair value estimate. artigo.texto: UPCL Invites Bids for 41 MW/102.5 MWh Battery Storage Projects 23 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Uttarakhand Power Corporation has invited bids to establish 41 MW/102.5 MWh of grid-interactive standalone Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) across six 33/11 kV substations in Uttarakhand. The projects will be developed under the Build-Own-Operate model through capacity charge-based competitive bidding, with Viability Gap Funding (VGF) support of up to Rs. 1.8 mn per MWh. The tender, numbered CCP-I/49/2026-2027, was issued on November 17, 2026. The pre-bid meeting is scheduled for November 26 at 11:30 am at UPCL’s Dehradun office, with online participation available. Bidders must submit queries by 5 pm on the same day through the designated tender email address. The combined capacity will be distributed across substations in Uttarkashi, Haridwar and Tehri districts. The identified locations are Kalyani and Dhanarigaad in Uttarkashi, SIDCUL Sector 8 and Jwalapur 2 in Haridwar, New Manglaur in Roorkee, and Rajakhet in Tehri. Individual project capacities range from 4 MW/10 MWh to 10 MW/25 MWh. Selected systems must complete two charge-discharge cycles daily. Each cycle will include 2.5 hours of discharge during the morning peak and another 2.5 hours during the evening peak. UPCL will provide land at its substations to successful developers under a Right of Use arrangement. The VGF assistance will be provided as non-recurring financial support and funded entirely by the central government. Developers will handle design, financing, supply, installation, commissioning, operations and maintenance. Projects must be commissioned within 12 months of the later of the effective date of the Battery Energy Storage Purchase Agreement (BESPA) or land handover, while the BESPA will run for 12 years after full commissioning. The tender requires an earnest money deposit of Rs. 41.3 mn, while the bid submission and opening schedules are set out in the Notice Inviting Tender. artigo.texto: Balmer Lawrie Invites Bids for 522 kWh BESS and Solar Project 23 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Balmer Lawrie & Co. has invited online bids to establish a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) integrated with a 600 kW solar power plant at its industrial packaging facility in Taloja, Navi Mumbai. The contract covers the supply, installation, testing and commissioning of a 522 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery storage system. The proposed BESS will store surplus electricity generated during daylight hours and supply it during the evening and periods of peak demand. The project is intended to improve solar power utilisation and strengthen energy management at the facility. The tender has been issued through the company’s e-procurement portal under reference number 0100PC3430. Eligible bidders must be registered entities with an average annual turnover of at least Rs. 9 mn during the financial years 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. They must also demonstrate experience in solar power execution, including at least one grid-connected solar installation with a capacity of 300 kW or higher. Bidders must be based in Mumbai or within approximately 200 km by road, maintain an office or authorised service centre in Maharashtra and hold a valid state electrical contractor licence. A site visit to the Taloja facility is mandatory, with bidders required to submit valid attendance proof. A gate pass alone will not be accepted. No advance payment will be made to the successful bidder. The tender was published on November 17, 2026, and proposals must be submitted by November 27 at 16:00 hours, with opening scheduled for 16:05 hours the same day. The selected bidder must confirm purchase-order acceptance within seven days and complete the project within 10 weeks of site clearance. The tender requires an Earnest Money Deposit of Rs. 45,000, although eligible Micro and Small Enterprises with valid registration are exempt. Security Deposit is set at 3 per cent of the basic order value, while 10 per cent of the total order value will be retained as performance security, subject to the stated release and guarantee conditions. artigo.texto: Juniper Green Commissions 108.50 MWp Solar and 94.77 MWh BESS 23 Nov 2026 2 Min Read CW Team Share Juniper Green Energy has commissioned capacities across two renewable energy projects through its subsidiaries. Juniper Green ETA Five has completed the entire 108.50 MWp solar component of a 75 MW wind-solar hybrid power project, while Juniper Green Stellar has commissioned a 94.77 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). Both commissioning activities took place at their respective project sites on November 19, 2026. The solar component forms part of a project being developed under a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company (MSEDCL). Juniper Green ETA Five, a wholly owned subsidiary of Juniper Green Energy, undertook the commissioning. The company disclosed the development through a regulatory filing. Juniper Green Stellar, another wholly owned subsidiary, commissioned the 94.77 MWh BESS as merchant capacity. The storage facility will initially operate in the merchant market, although the subsidiary retains the option of transferring the capacity to a long-term PPA in the future. Earlier this year, Juniper Green Energy fully commissioned a 100 MWh merchant BESS project at Bikaner in Rajasthan through its subsidiary Juniper Green Cosmic. The project is among the first operational merchant BESS facilities in India. The company also completed a 150 MW wind-solar hybrid project awarded by Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam after commissioning its final 5 MW wind turbine. The 150 MW hybrid project was secured through the greenshoe option under a 500 MW tender issued by Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam. Juniper Green received the project at a tariff of Rs. 3.04/kWh, while KPI Green Energy secured a 50 MW project at Rs. 2.99/kWh. The latest commissioning adds to Juniper Green Energy’s operating renewable generation and storage portfolio. artigo.texto: Data centers: expansÃ£o tecnolÃ³gica esbarra em dilemas econÃ´micos e socioambientais Setor empresarial defende fortalecimento da soberania digital, enquanto pesquisadores e entidades questionam a geraÃ§Ã£o de empregos e os custos socioambientais Publicado: 21/11/2026 Ã s 08:00 Os data centers sÃ£o criticados, entre outros motivos, pelo elevado consumo de energia e Ã¡gua (DIVULGAÃÃO/GOV.BR) A infraestrutura necessária para a expansão tecnológica no Brasil é um dos grandes dilemas atuais que envolvem o poder público, a sociedade civil e o setor empresarial. No centro do debate estão os data centers, conjuntos de equipamentos que funcionam como o “cérebro” físico de toda a rede mundial de computadores. De um lado, apoiadores defendem a criação de empregos e o reforço da soberania digital frente às big techs estrangeiras. Do outro, críticos apontam que os supostos benefícios não compensariam os impactos socioambientais causados. De acordo com a Associação Brasileira de Data Center (ABDC), a expectativa é de que o setor de data centers atraia até R$ 1 trilhão em investimentos até 2036. Os números serão possíveis a partir de políticas de desoneração como o Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata), sancionado pelo Governo Federal em setembro deste ano, que prevê a isenção de impostos de importação na aquisição de equipamentos destinados aos data centers. Um relatório da agência de classificação de risco estadunidense Moody’s, divulgado em janeiro deste ano, aponta que o Brasil ocupa o 12º lugar no ranking global de data centers. No contexto da América Latina, o país lidera em número de empreendimentos com quase 200 data centers, metade da quantidade de estruturas em funcionamento na região. A maior parte se concentra na região Sudeste, mais especificamente nos estados de São Paulo e Rio de Janeiro. Em Pernambuco, a instalação de um data center em Paranatama, município com uma população aproximada de 12 mil pessoas no Agreste do estado, chegou a receber a licença da Agência Estadual de Meio Ambiente (CPRH). Porém, a mobilização de entidades da sociedade civil e as mudanças no processo de licenciamento para empreendimentos do tipo aprovadas pelo Conselho Nacional do Meio Ambiente (Conama) fizeram a empresa recuar. A desistência do projeto foi anunciada pelo Ministério Público de Pernambuco (MPPE), no último dia 11 de novembro, em audiência pública convocada para debater o tema. Em um evento de tecnologia no início do mês, a governadora Raquel Lyra ponderou os impactos da atração dos empreendimentos para os recursos naturais do estado, em especial sobre o fornecimento de água. “Lido com o El Niño, com a racionalização da água, e tenho que instalar data center. Tenho um polo cervejeiro, um polo de jeans e vou usar minha água onde? Os recursos são escassos”, afirmou. A gestora também questionou o retorno econômico e a geração de empregos frente ao investimento necessário. Durante a campanha eleitoral deste ano, o tema já havia sido abordado por João Campos, candidato derrotado na corrida pelo Executivo estadual. Em entrevistas e sabatinas, o ex-prefeito do Recife criticou a suposta falta de articulação da gestão atual na atração dos investimentos, citando como exemplo a instalação de um data center da empresa ByteDance, proprietária da plataforma TikTok, no município de Caucaia, na Região Metropolitana de Fortaleza. Geração de empregos e retorno econômico A mão de obra envolvida na instalação de um data center se distribui entre os trabalhadores que executam as obras de construção da infraestrutura física, os postos ocupados durante a operação do empreendimento e outros setores envolvidos de forma secundária nas atividades. De acordo com um levantamento da Fundação Getúlio Vargas (FGV), um único data center de 100 megawatts para operações de inteligência artificial pode envolver um investimento total de R$ 25 bilhões e gerar cerca de 12,5 mil empregos diretos e indiretos, sendo 10,7 mil temporários e 1,8 mil permanentes. Para o advogado André Fernandes, fundador e pesquisador líder do Instituto de Pesquisa em Direito e Tecnologia do Recife (IP.rec), a injeção de vagas no mercado de trabalho não seria suficiente para compensar os impactos socioambientais dos empreendimentos. Ele compara com outros empreendimentos locais, como a Refinaria Abreu e Lima e o Estaleiro Atlântico Sul, que teriam mobilizado uma quantidade maior de trabalhadores nas etapas de edificação. “É uma obra de engenharia civil muito mais simples. A estrutura de construção civil é um galpão de concreto pré-moldado com a instalação de toda uma parafernália elétrica de resfriamento, com ou sem água. Você não tem toda essa geração de emprego. O questionamento que nossos mandantes deveriam fazer é se faz sentido, para economia, o tipo de investimento e as consequências de médio e longo prazo. A nível indireto e direto, são pouquíssimos empregos”, apontou. O professor Abraham Sicsú, doutor em Economia, aponta a necessidade de observar o fenômeno do ponto de vista qualitativo, além de considerar estratégias como o powershoring, que propõe a instalação de empreendimentos de alto consumo energético em regiões com oferta abundante de energias renováveis. “Embora o data center em si não gere muito emprego, com o powershoring e com a cadeia de suprimentos, você passa a ter setores significativamente empregantes e com emprego mais qualificado, mais tecnificado e com melhores salários. Então melhora a qualidade da empregabilidade”, avaliou. Já o presidente do Porto Digital, Pierre Lucena, pondera a necessidade de analisar com cautela a construção dos empreendimentos ligados às big techs, que possuem requisitos diferenciados. “Precisamos distinguir a infraestrutura que atende às empresas locais daquela voltada, principalmente, às demandas de grandes plataformas globais. São investimentos com impactos econômicos diferentes, que precisam ser avaliados individualmente”, afirmou. Impactos socioambientais Os data centers são

artigo.texto: Em parceria inédita com a AKAD Seguros e estruturada com a corretora Marsh, a climatech brasileira eleva o padrão de integridade e blindará 100% das suas emissões contra falhas na entrega, riscos de projetos e greenwashing Em um movimento pioneiro para sanar o principal gargalo de confiança do mercado de ativos ambientais, a Greenline, multinacional brasileira de tecnologia climática, anuncia a adoção de apólice de seguro obrigatória para a totalidade dos créditos de carbono mensurados e emitidos em suas operações. A solução foi desenvolvida e estruturada com o apoio da corretora internacional Marsh e comercializada pela AKAD Seguros. A iniciativa responde à crescente exigência de grandes compradores globais por segurança jurídica, financeira e reputacional diante de controvérsias sobre a integridade e a permanência de projetos de conservação florestal. Com a nova política, a Greenline passa a ser a primeira empresa a exigir cobertura securitária como pré-requisito indispensável para a emissão de créditos ex-post, emitidos após verificação dos resultados. O seguro cobrirá quatro frentes críticas de risco que costumam travar grandes transações no mercado voluntário: falha na entrega dos créditos de carbono contratados; falha estrutural do projeto responsável pela geração; perda permanente de utilidade dos ativos, inclusive desqualificação de metodologias ou autorizações governamentais; e custos adicionais para a aquisição de créditos substitutos no mercado caso os ativos originais sofram sinistros ou desqualificação. A apólice prevê ainda a cobertura de despesas emergenciais estratégicas para a mitigação de danos, como custos imediatos com combate a incêndios florestais e realização de auditorias de urgência após desastres naturais. O parâmetro inicial estabelecido é de US$ 25 milhões em limite de cobertura por projeto. Tomando como referência o preço médio de US$ 10 por crédito, cada projeto segurado pela Greenline poderá contar com proteção equivalente a 2,5 milhões de toneladas de gás carbônicos. “Controvérsias sobre a qualidade dos créditos, regularidade fundiária e o risco reputacional do greenwashing tornaram-se tópicos centrais em nossas negociações com grandes compradores corporativos. Tornar o seguro obrigatório em 100% das nossas operações não é apenas uma garantia financeira. É uma declaração de maturidade do setor. Estamos transformando ativos ambientais em instrumentos financeiros verdadeiramente bancáveis“, destaca Lucio Lopez, fundador e CEO da Greenline. Padrão metodológico permite retrospectiva de carteira Além das novas emissões, a cobertura securitária também poderá contemplar projetos que já eram mensurados pela Greenline antes da parceria formal com a AKAD, sujeitos à avaliação de risco da seguradora. A viabilidade dessa extensão decorre da padronização tecnológica e dos rigorosos processos de mensuração via sensoriamento remoto mantidos pela climatech. Desenvolvida focado na preservação de florestas nativas e redução de desmatamento, a solução foi concebida para atender o mercado de forma ampla. A Greenline atuou como articuladora da demanda, mas o produto também estará disponível para outros agentes do setor de ativos ambientais conforme critérios da AKAD. artigo.texto: BYD's Hybrid Slump Sets the Bar for Ti9 as Legal and Brokerage Headwinds Pile Up Published on 11/21/2026 at 17:40 | Editorial boerse-global.de A Dutch court's ruling against the BYD Ti7, two trimmed price targets and a flagship launch meant to plug a hybrid-sized hole — the past few days have handed BYD investors plenty to digest at once. The legal setback came first. A court in the Netherlands ruled yesterday that sales of the Ti7 must stop across the European Union, according to Reuters, after concluding the model infringes the design of Jaguar Land Rover's Defender. BYD shares slipped 3.6% on the session to close at €7.05. Analysts were already moving in the same direction. Daiwa cut its target for BYD's H-shares to HK$100 from HK$119 yesterday while keeping its buy rating, pointing to weaker demand in the company's Chinese home market than it had expected for the final quarter. The brokerage also trimmed its earnings forecasts, by 7% for 2026 and 9% for 2027. Bank of America Securities had gone earlier, lowering its own target to HK$104 from HK$124 on Wednesday, with its buy recommendation left intact. A 200,000-Vehicle Hole in the Hybrid Book The demand softness Daiwa flags is visible most clearly in plug-in hybrids. BYD sold roughly 200,000 fewer plug-in hybrid passenger cars in the first ten months of this year than in the same stretch of 2024. From January through October the company moved just over 1.6 million plug-in hybrids, down from more than 1.8 million a year earlier — a decline of 11%. Sales of new-energy vehicles as a whole fell only about 2% over the period, to some 3.6 million from 3.7 million, so the weakness is concentrated rather than spread evenly across the range. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? October itself offered a brighter picture. BYD reported around 490,000 new-energy vehicle sales for the month, up 11% from roughly 442,000 a year earlier. All of these figures come from the company's monthly release and are unaudited. Even so, the year-to-date shortfall stands, and it is steepest in hybrids. Fang Cheng Bao's Flagship Arrives That is the gap the Ti9 is driving into. Fang Cheng Bao, BYD's group brand, announced the launch date of 19 November via its Weibo account on 17 November, with reservations in China open since 9 November, as Sina Auto reported at the time. The Ti9 is the brand's flagship and sits on BYD's DMS hybrid platform, placing it squarely in the segment that is struggling. One model at the top of a brand will hardly erase a shortfall of about 200,000 vehicles on its own. It does not have to, either, to give the hybrid business a meaningful lift. Why the Shortfall Is No Benchmark Spread across ten months, the gap works out to just over 20,000 vehicles a month. Treating that figure as a hurdle for the Ti9 would be a mistake: it describes what BYD has on average been missing so far, not how many extra hybrids the group must sell each month going forward. That depends on how the rest of the hybrid line-up performs — and on how many Ti9s Fang Cheng Bao actually delivers. The number is a backward-looking average and says nothing about sales of the new model. BYD at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Separately, BYD Battery and Beijing Bus Media signed a memorandum of understanding yesterday covering battery management across the full life cycle, vehicle sales and related services, as well as advertising and brand promotion. The picture is thus clearer than it first appears, though only halfway. Hybrids are the group's weak spot, and the Ti9 is aimed precisely there. How much it can fix will be settled by its unit sales and by the trajectory of the other hybrid models — not by a historical shortfall. artigo.texto: HiTHIUM Debuts Integrated C&I Microgrid Solution to Enhance Energy Management and Power Reliability LAS VEGAS, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On November 18, at RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas, HiTHIUM unveiled its first integrated microgrid solution designed for commercial and industrial (C&I) applications, highlighting its latest innovations in energy storage integration and microgrid energy management. Centered on the âPower 1,022kWh liquid-cooled C&I energy storage system, the solution integrates energy storage and energy management technologies to enable coordinated control and flexible dispatch of multiple energy sources, supporting both daily energy optimization and backup power needs. On-site Presentation Highlights HiTHIUM's C&I Microgrid Innovations During the event, Gary Gu, Technical Director at HiTHIUM, presented the company's technology roadmap and integrated solutions for the C&I microgrid market. His presentation covered the development of the U.S. microgrid market, key system components and their applications across different scenarios. He also introduced the solution's core architecture, featuring C&I energy storage systems, grid-forming power conversion systems (PCS), grid-connected/off-grid switching equipment and microgrid controllers. He explained how these components work together with energy management systems and other energy sources to address the diverse needs of C&I facilities, from everyday energy management to backup power supply. Integrated System Design for Energy Optimization and Backup Power At the core of the solution is the âPower liquid-cooled DC energy storage system, with a rated capacity of approximately 1,022kWh per cabinet. The system integrates PCS, grid-connected/off-grid switching equipment and a microgrid controller, with the flexibility to incorporate on-site solar PV and backup generators based on project requirements. During normal grid-connected operation, the system can store surplus solar power or charge batteries during off-peak electricity hours and discharge during peak periods. This helps reduce peak grid demand, support peak shaving and load shifting, and optimize electricity costs. Meanwhile, the energy management system can reserve battery capacity for critical loads, allowing facility operators to balance daily energy optimization with backup power requirements based on their operational priorities. Seamless Grid Transition to Help Protect Critical Loads For C&I facilities such as cold storage warehouses and food processing plants, unexpected power outages can disrupt operations and affect critical equipment. When the utility grid is interrupted, the solution can safely disconnect from the grid through its switching equipment, provided the system is configured for off-grid operation. It then coordinates available battery storage and other power sources to supply designated critical loads. At RE+ 2026, HiTHIUM demonstrated this capability through an interactive model simulating a power outage at a cold storage facility. Once disconnected from the utility grid, the microgrid prioritized power supply to refrigeration equipment while dynamically adjusting EV charging power based on available electricity, demonstrating flexible energy allocation and load management during an outage. HiTHIUM also works with facility operators, engineering teams and system integrators to tailor system power and capacity to specific project requirements, taking into account load profiles, critical equipment and target backup durations. Actual switching performance and backup duration depend on system configuration, available battery capacity, on-site generation and load demand. By integrating energy storage, power conversion and intelligent energy management, HiTHIUM's integrated C&I microgrid solution provides a flexible approach to both everyday energy optimization and backup power. Looking ahead, HiTHIUM will continue to advance energy storage technologies and their applications, delivering integrated solutions that help C&I customers improve energy efficiency and power reliability. SOURCE HiTHIUM

artigo.texto: Polarium Energy Solutions AB, a Sweden-based maker of lithium-ion energy storage systems, has been declared bankrupt by the Stockholm District Court. The application was filed on 20 November 2026, and the court accepted it on the same day. Mikael Kubu of Ackordscentralen has been appointed as the trustee, and he is to decide whether the business should be sold or kept running. Polarium has blamed battery prices that have fallen sharply under competition from Chinese suppliers. Telecom operators had cut their investments, and some of its distributed BESS projects had been delayed. The company had more than halved its operating expenses since 2024, but it had not been able to find a buyer. Harald Mix, the chairman, has put more than SEK 350 million (~ $34.37 million) into Polarium through his investment company. He is now to ask the trustee whether the most viable parts of the business can be carried forward. Swedish battery storage maker Polarium is declared bankrupt After it had cited falling battery prices and weak telecom demand, Polarium has been declared bankrupt and a trustee is to decide whether it should be sold. artigo.texto: A JA ESS lançou uma plataforma própria de passaporte de baterias, desenvolvida para gerenciar informações ao longo de todo o ciclo de vida dos produtos e ajudar as empresas a se p 20 de novembro de 2026, às 17:12 PEQUIM, 20 de novembro de 2026 /PRNewswire/ — A JA ESS lançou uma plataforma própria de passaporte de baterias, desenvolvida para gerenciar informações ao longo de todo o ciclo de vida dos produtos e ajudar as empresas a se prepararem para as próximas exigências regulatórias da União Europeia. A plataforma é hospedada no próprio ambiente de nuvem da empresa, permitindo que sua equipe assuma diretamente a responsabilidade pelas políticas de dados, pelas permissões de acesso e pelas futuras atualizações. Nos termos do Regulamento de Baterias da União Europeia, o passaporte de baterias será obrigatório, a partir de 18 de fevereiro de 2027, para baterias de meios de transporte leves (LMT), veículos elétricos e baterias industriais com capacidade superior a 2 kWh colocadas no mercado ou em serviço. Outros requisitos serão introduzidos posteriormente. O passaporte de baterias é um registro digital vinculado a uma bateria física específica. Um código QR e um identificador exclusivo baseado na série de normas ISO/IEC 15459 vinculam o registro à bateria e permitem acessar informações sobre todo o seu ciclo de vida. Essas informações podem incluir a identificação do produto, a composição dos materiais, a pegada de carbono, o conteúdo reciclado, o desempenho e a durabilidade, o estado de saúde da bateria, a devida diligência na cadeia de suprimentos e o tratamento no fim da vida útil. Em conjunto, esses dados permitem gerenciar as informações de forma consistente, desde a identificação do produto até o fim de sua vida útil. Para os fabricantes, o desafio não é simplesmente criar um código QR. Os dados devem ser rastreáveis até sua origem, mantidos atualizados e disponibilizados de acordo com os requisitos regulamentares e comerciais. As empresas também precisam controlar o acesso a informações confidenciais e observar as regras relativas à transferência internacional de dados e à proteção de segredos comerciais. Esse equilíbrio é especialmente relevante para empresas que atuam em diversos mercados. Quando as empresas utilizam plataformas de terceiros, suas funcionalidades, as permissões de acesso aos campos de dados e a interoperabilidade podem ficar condicionadas às configurações e ao modelo de prestação de serviços do provedor. A JA ESS desenvolveu a plataforma internamente e a hospeda em seu próprio ambiente de nuvem. As políticas de dados, as permissões de acesso e as futuras atualizações da plataforma ficam sob a responsabilidade da equipe interna da JA ESS. A solução atende aos requisitos da União Europeia relativos ao acesso, à apresentação e à atualização de dados, ao mesmo tempo que garante à JA ESS maior controle sobre sua gestão. A plataforma também poderá ser aprimorada à medida que os requisitos regulatórios evoluírem e sua aplicação prática proporcionar novos aprendizados. A JA ESS é a unidade de negócios de armazenamento de energia da marca JA. Como parte central da estratégia de armazenamento de energia da JA, a JA ESS atende a diversas aplicações FTM e BTM, oferecendo soluções seguras, eficientes, inteligentes e personalizadas para os segmentos de geração em larga escala, comercial e industrial e residencial. artigo.texto: The Lead In: Albert Lea water expansion, Olympic Torch Relay, Mitchell County data centers, moving forward in Winneshiek, and watching Twin Lakes ROCHESTER, Minn. (KTTC) – A massive expansion project. Bringing the Olympics to Freeborn County. Mitchell County talks data centers. Winneshiek County plans after mass resignations. And Twin Lakes prepares to learn its financial fate. Here is The Lead In, for Nov. 22-28. Albert Lea: Water and sewer extension City staff will present the council with a plan to extend water and sewer services to the area around Richway Drive/County Road 20 and Plaza Street in 2027. The $3.3 million project would improve failing septic systems and water pressure. It also would give industrial lots in the area access to city water. The city would pay for the project through sewer and water funds, state aid, property assessments and bonding. The project also would annex several properties into the city. The council meets at 7 p.m. Monday in the council chambers. Albert Lea: Olympic torch relay agreement The council will also vote on approving an agreement between Albert Lea and the Los Angeles Organizing Committee for the Olympic Games 2028 to participate in the Olympic torch run. The run for the 2028 Summer Games will cover all 50 states. The city is seeking consideration for the relay route. The agreement does not guarantee Albert Lea will be on the route. The process is in preliminary stages. City staff said the opportunity is too good to pass up. Again, the council meets at 7 p.m. Monday in the council chambers. Mitchell County: Data center moratorium The Mitchell County Board of Supervisors is scheduled to discuss a data center moratorium Tuesday. The item is listed on the board’s regular meeting agenda. In November 2025, the board issued a data center moratorium through Dec. 31, 2026. The vote was 4-1. It is unclear what action, if any, the board will take Tuesday, including whether it will extend or change the existing ordinance. The meeting begins at 8:30 a.m. Tuesday at the Mitchell County Courthouse in Osage. Winneshiek County: Discussing recent planning and zoning resignations The Winneshiek County Board of Supervisors is set to meet for the first time since every member of the county planning and zoning commission resigned in protest. The board’s Monday agenda indicates it will discuss the resignations. Former commissioners said they quit after supervisors declined to reappoint Mary Hoffman, who wants to keep serving after more than 15 years. They said tensions had built for years. They said supervisors, who have the final say on rezoning requests, did not give the commission’s recommendations enough consideration. Five former members said they will return if Hoffman is reinstated and Supervisor Mark Vick resigns by the end of the year. Former Chair Wendy Stevens said two new members have been appointed, but four are needed to conduct business. She said work on a proposed data center ordinance was about halfway done. The Board of Supervisors meets at 9:30 a.m. Monday in the Courthouse annex in Decorah. Twin Lakes: State aid on the line for the final time More than $40,000 in state aid is at stake in Twin Lakes, Minnesota. The city had until Friday to submit required financial reporting from 2025. KTTC reached out to the State Auditor’s Office for an update. The office said it will follow up Monday. KTTC also attempted to get a response from Twin Lakes City Clerk and Treasurer Keith Haskell. The reports were due in March. The state offered additional deadlines, which the city continued to miss. Haskell has previously said he was unable to submit the reports because of mismanagement issues by the former city clerk. Find stories like this and more, in our apps. Copyright 2026 KTTC. artigo.texto: Stifel Says SpaceX Could Buy Stalled Data Centers for One Reason: Their Power. Here’s Why Electricity Is the Real Asset. There is increasing pushback against AI because of its impact on the power grid, but that's also an opportunity. By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Key Points - Stifel analyst Jonathan Siegmann recently suggested that SpaceX could acquire stalled data centers. - The key trigger for such an acquisition would be data centers that already have power. - As pushback against AI data centers grows, electricity becomes an increasingly important factor for investors to consider. Wall Street analysts can only make educated guesses, just like every other investor. But they do have an advantage since they are often industry experts. This is why Stifel analyst Jonathan Siegmann's suggestion that Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) could buy up stalled data centers is so interesting. The key theme, however, is that SpaceX will likely only be interested in data centers that already have dedicated power. Here's why this is so important and what it could mean for your stock selection process as you look at companies like Bloom Energy (BE -15.30%), NextEra Energy (NEE -0.41%), and Brookfield Renewable (BEP -2.97%). SpaceX sees the problem very clearly SpaceX has a large AI data center in Memphis that it has dubbed Colossus. It is a huge asset, and it uses massive amounts of power. To ensure there is enough electricity to run the data center, SpaceX built its own dedicated natural-gas power plant. Local residents aren't happy about this, but it highlights that SpaceX is clearly aware of the power problem posed by AI data centers. Image source: Getty Images. As the backlash against AI data centers grows, access to electricity is becoming an increasingly important and contentious issue. Which is why Stifel analyst Jonathan Siegmann thinks SpaceX could end up buying data centers that have dedicated power agreements in place. However, you don't need to play this specific angle to benefit. Increasingly, AI companies are being forced to supply their own power. And there are a handful of companies that look set to benefit, including Bloom Energy, NextEra Energy, and Brookfield Renewable. Bloom Energy is a high risk/high reward option Bloom Energy makes hydrogen fuel cells. Notably, each fuel cell it sells comes along with a long-term service contract, creating an annuity-like income stream. The company's products are factory-built and can be easily deployed wherever they are needed, providing off-grid power. The company has been losing money for years but is likely to be profitable in 2026. That could be an important inflection point for the business. BE Bloom Energy NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26 But investors are well aware of the opportunity, pushing the stock higher by more than 1,200% over the past three years. With a lofty price-to-earnings ratio of roughly 100x, it is very clearly a well-loved stock. And yet, the opportunity to power AI data centers remains substantial, and perhaps only getting larger. If you are an aggressive growth investor, you should at least consider Bloom Energy, even if you only end up adding it to your wish list. NextEra Energy covers two bases NextEra Energy is one of the world's largest utilities. In fact, it is looking to get even bigger, with its proposed acquisition of Dominion Energy (D -0.56%). Notably, Dominion's regulated electricity operations include one of the world's most important data center markets. The pairing will also vault NextEra into the number two spot with regard to U.S. nuclear power generation. Basically, NextEra looks like it is doubling down on electricity demand and AI at the same time. NEE NextEra Energy NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26 But there's an interesting twist here. NextEra is well positioned to benefit from data centers that get attached to the grid. However, it is also one of the world's largest producers of solar and wind power, a business that falls outside of the regulated framework. So it can also sell power directly to AI customers under long-term contracts. For more conservative investors, NextEra could be an attractive way to play AI's power demand, both from within and outside the regulated framework. You'll also get to collect NextEra's well-above-market 2.9% dividend yield. Brookfield Renewable is focused on clean energy For investors looking to maximize the income they generate, Brookfield Renewable and its 5.2% may be even more attractive. The partnership is focused on clean energy, but has a surprisingly diversified portfolio. For starters, it operates hydroelectric, solar, and wind power facilities. It has increasingly been investing in battery storage. And it owns half of Westinghouse, which is one of the world's largest service providers to the nuclear power industry. artigo.texto: Data centers se tornam alvos estratégicos de guerra Infraestrutura de computação é responsável pela comunicação e funcionamento em diversos serviços essenciais. A ameaça de Donald Trump de impedir empresas americanas de construir data centers fora dos EUA abre novo capítulo do protecionismo digital, na disputa por hegemonia com a China. Pode prejudicar perspectivas de investimentos no Brasil e dificultar a regulação. Data centers reúnem milhares de servidores e processadores e exigem investimentos bilionários. São essenciais para treinar e operar modelos de IA. Trump já havia, no dia 16, submetido a licença especial o fornecimento dos chips mais sofisticados para o Brasil, Indonésia, Malásia, Singapura e Tailândia. Os EUA restringem a venda dos chips mais avançados da Nvidia a empresas chinesas. Mas, instalados em terceiros países, esses processadores podem ter sua capacidade computacional contratada remotamente por clientes chienes. Data centers geram negócios para a construção civil, fabricantes de equipamentos, empresas de energia e telecomunicações, além de empregos especializados. Trump deseja manter esses investimentos nos EUA. A medida, porém, pode ter o efeito contrário ao esperado. Empresas escolhem onde instalar essas estruturas considerando custo da energia, conectividade, proximidade dos usuários e regras sobre dados. Obrigá-las a operar nos EUA pode elevar custos e reduzir eficiência. A matriz elétrica limpa e o baixo risco geopolítico são atrativos para a instalação de data centers no Brasil. Uma restrição efetiva poderia afastar projetos de empresas americanas. Não arraria investimentos brasileiros, europeus ou chineses, mas reduziria sua competitividade. A execução é incerta. Trump ameaçou impor tributação elevada a empresas que construam data centers no exterior, mas não detalhou alíquotas, alcance ou fundamento jurídico. A criação de tributos federais cabe ao Congresso. A proliferação dos data centers levou a derrotas dos republicanos nas eleições demeio de mandato, por causa do aumento do custo da eletricidade. A maioria democrata no Congresso poderá se opor a essa política. Leia mais - Como data centers se tornaram novos alvos estratégicos de guerra: ‘Brilham como árvores de Natal’ - Boom de datacenters deve influenciar eleição legislativa em Estados decisivos nos EUA A infraestrutura digital passa a ser tratada como questão de segurança nacional -- o expediente de Trump para adotar decisões sem consultar o Congresso dominado pelos democratas a partir de 3 de janeiro. O escopo da disputa com os chineses é ampliado dos chips e algoritmos para o acesso à capacidade computacional. Ao tentar proteger sua liderança, os EUA tendem a intensificar a fragmentação da economia digital. A China terá ainda mais incentivo para desenvolver infraestrutura e tecnologia próprias, reduzir dependências e criar um mundo digital dividido em blocos rivais. Ficará ainda mais difícil regular a IA.

artigo.texto: Inside Ola Electric's battery manufacturing journey: How it makes 4680 Bharat Cells and plans to reduce China's dependence Ola's Krishnagiri Gigafactory has 6 GWh of commissioned annual capacity, with infrastructure that can accommodate 20 GWh. The company reported NMC manufacturing yields closer to 80% and says its 4680 cell retained 90% capacity after 1,000 charge-discharge cycles. Ola is developing LFP, LMFP, sodium-ion and solid-state batteries while working to reduce its dependence on imported materials. India's ambition to become a global battery manufacturing hub faces a challenge that goes beyond setting up factories: building a domestic supply chain for the materials and technologies required to manufacture cells at scale. While the country has developed capabilities in battery pack design, battery management systems (BMS) and vehicle integration, several critical materials and manufacturing inputs still come from overseas. Ola Electric is among the companies attempting to address this gap. Its Gigafactory in Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu, has 6 GWh of commissioned annual manufacturing capacity, where the company produces its 4680 Bharat Cell. It is also developing LFP batteries and researching newer chemistries, including LMFP, sodium-ion and solid-state batteries. However, manufacturing cells in India does not necessarily mean the entire process is localised. The company continues to import cathode and anode active materials and some precision equipment. In an interaction with Digit, an Ola Electric spokesperson discussed its manufacturing process, dependence on China, battery safety, recycling and what India needs to become more self-reliant in battery technology. How Ola manufactures its 4680 Bharat Cell At the Ola Gigafactory, battery manufacturing begins with active-material powders, which are converted into electrode films using the company's dry process. These films are laminated onto metal foils, cut into strips and wound together with a separator between the electrodes. The winding is then placed inside a metal can, followed by welding, electrolyte filling and sealing. The assembled cells undergo their first controlled charge before being tested and graded. They are subsequently used in battery packs assembled at Ola's Futurefactory. Explaining the process, the spokesperson said, "At the Ola Gigafactory, we turn active-material powders into electrode films using our dry process. We laminate the films onto metal foils, cut them into strips and wind them with a separator between the electrodes." However, several inputs still come from outside India. Ola imports cathode and anode active materials and some precision equipment, while separators are sourced from specialist suppliers. The company says it has localised electrolyte and some mechanical components, with a near-term target of achieving more than 60% localisation. China dependence and the search for alternative suppliers China remains an important part of the global battery supply chain, particularly in refining lithium into battery-grade chemicals and processing graphite used in anodes. Although countries such as Australia, Chile and Argentina also produce lithium, developing domestic refining capabilities remains important for India's battery ambitions. Ola says it has qualified suppliers outside China for key raw materials to reduce the risk of supply disruptions. Its electrode materials currently come from China, Japan and South Korea. The company is also validating Indian-made lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode material. The spokesperson said, "We have already qualified suppliers outside China for key raw materials. That gives us a tested alternative before a disruption." Rare-earth supply concerns have also influenced its motor development. Ola says the situation accelerated the development of its certified ferrite motor, which does not use rare-earth magnets. NMC, LFP and next-generation battery technologies Ola is developing different battery chemistries for different applications. Its 4680 Bharat Cell uses nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) chemistry, which the company considers suitable for scooters, motorcycles and other vehicles that need higher energy density within limited space. For affordable electric vehicles and stationary energy storage, Ola is focusing on LFP chemistry because of its lower cost and long cycle life. Its 46100 LFP cell has received Bureau of Indian Standards certification, with vehicle integration targeted around March or April 2027. The company is also developing higher-energy NMC and manganese-enriched LFP (LMFP) batteries. Sodium-ion and solid-state technologies, however, remain at the laboratory stage. "Sodium-ion is a candidate for stationary storage, where weight matters less. We have no firm volume-production dates for these programmes," the spokesperson said. The next challenge for these technologies is demonstrating cycle life and consistent performance on a production line rather than just in laboratory testing. Why scaling cell manufacturing remains difficult Moving from laboratory experiments to high-volume manufacturing is one of the biggest challenges for battery companies. Ola says maintaining uniformity across an entire electrode roll while operating at production speed has been particularly difficult. A roll may meet its average coating target, but a section along the edge of the cathode could still have insufficient active material. Cells manufactured using that portion may consequently store less charge. Identifying such variations early can prevent wasted material, electricity and machine time. The spokesperson explained, "The hardest step has been keeping an entire electrode roll uniform at production speed." Ola reported that its NMC manufacturing yield was closer to 80% in November. artigo.texto: Ginlong Technologies invested 544 million yuan in the transition from photovoltaic power curtailment to energy storage investment, tearing up the old account books of photovoltaic power plants. Is energy storage the answer to everything? New energy capital flows between the photovoltaic and energy storage tracks following the revenue model. According to Energy Insight, on the evening of November 20, Ginlong Technologies announced that its board of directors has terminated the "Distributed Photovoltaic Power Station Project", which was originally planned to invest 354 million yuan, and not a single penny had been invested as of November 13; the company reallocated 189 million yuan from two inverter projects, pooling 544 million yuan to shift the investment to an annual 8GWh energy storage system production line. Prior to this, Zoomlion Energy also carried out similar capital reallocation, while other enterprises transferred the remaining funds from energy storage back to the photovoltaic sector. The back-and-forth flow of capital between the two tracks is far more complicated than just the rotation of industry trends: the electricity pricing mechanism, grid connection rules and revenue models have all been rewritten at the same time. The rooftop remains the same, but the checkout counter has adopted a completely new settlement method. The rooftop project accounts no longer add up at first When the Document No.136 was implemented on February 9, 2025, what was truly rewritten was not the subsidy figure, but the most valuable part of the revenue of new energy power stations — certainty. The National Development and Reform Commission and the National Energy Administration divided new energy projects into two categories: existing projects and new projects, based on the cutoff date of June 1 of that year. The former will follow the current policy for benchmark electricity prices, which will not be higher than the local coal-fired power benchmark price, while the latter will enter provincial bidding, and the electricity included in the mechanism will be adjusted up or down according to the difference between the market price and the benchmark mechanism price. The mechanism electricity price is not a fixed purchase price, but a contract for difference. In the past, the "electricity sales revenue" line in the calculation sheet was a fixed figure, but now it is split into two parts: electricity under the mechanism and market revenue outside the mechanism. The monthly rent-like certainty in the past has been broken down into hourly prices. The inflection point of the installed capacity curve appeared in the data earlier than in the announcements, and the statistics from the National Energy Administration clearly depict this trend. In 2024, China's new installed photovoltaic capacity reached 278 million kilowatts, which rose to 317 million kilowatts in 2025, while the figure for the first three quarters of 2026 was 110.33 million kilowatts, down 53.9% year on year. The new photovoltaic mechanism electricity price in Shanghai is 0.4155 yuan per kWh, 0.225 yuan per kWh in Shandong, and the 2026 figure in Xinjiang falls at the lower limit of 0.15 yuan per kWh, meaning different provinces no longer follow the same accounting standard. BloombergNEF estimates that the actual market electricity price for photovoltaic power is on average 0.127 yuan per kWh lower than the mechanism electricity price. In Shandong, the average spot trading price of photovoltaic power in February 2025 once dropped to only 0.057 yuan per kWh, and there were about 1330 hours of negative electricity prices in the spot market for the whole year, nearly half of which were concentrated in spring. The stronger the sun shines, the lower the price goes. The decline in yield is not an abstract curve in research reports, it soon fell on specific people and projects. According to media reports, the internal rate of return of distributed industrial and commercial projects was originally about 13% to 14%, which dropped to 8% to 9% after the issuance of Document No.136. A person in charge of a distributed photovoltaic project in Shandong said that he has suspended investing in new projects since May 31. The aforementioned project of Ginlong Technologies was originally planned to be connected to the grid by the end of 2026, which already belongs to the category of new projects. The zero investment does not mean capital shortage, but a halt after the accounts no longer add up. The suspended fundraising project is equivalent to the financial model casting a vote of no confidence first. With no mandatory supporting orders, the energy storage sector has to seek business on its own The fundraising change plan of Zoomlion Energy in February 2025 is most easily interpreted by the outside world as a simple track switching story. It reduced the fundraising for the distributed photovoltaic power station project from 700 million yuan to 450 million yuan, with 250 million yuan returned to the capital pool. In the same plan, the renamed and expanded energy storage project is proposed to invest 690 million yuan, which is even lower than the original 800 million yuan. The so-called "abandoning photovoltaic for energy storage" in most cases does not mean taking one yuan from the photovoltaic sector and putting it directly into the energy storage sector, but reordering the capital in the overall plate. The reason why capital shifts to the battery sector is not that the battery sector is better at telling stories, but that it has begun to have independent and accountable cash flow. Document No.136 clearly stipulates that allocating energy storage shall not be taken as a precondition for the approval and grid connection of new energy projects, so energy storage power stations that used to make a living by leasing capacity once had no buyers. artigo.texto: BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 23. The State Oil Company of Azerbaijan (SOCAR) is exploring opportunities to introduce new energy storage technologies and improve the resilience of the country's power system, SOCAR Vice President Afgan Isayev said on Monday at the Azerbaijan-Italy Business Forum in Baku, Trend's correspondent reports. According to him, existing power grids cannot accommodate unlimited amounts of electricity from variable-output renewable energy sources, making grid modernization necessary. "In this regard, technologies such as sodium-ion and vanadium flow batteries are being considered. Energy storage systems play an important role in enabling the integration of renewable energy sources into power grids," he said. He also highlighted the development of sodium-ion batteries in China, noting that the technology could become more affordable due to the widespread availability of sodium and have a lower environmental impact than lithium batteries. According to SOCAR's vice president, the company is exploring opportunities to integrate such technologies into Azerbaijan's national power system in cooperation with AREA, the Ministry of Energy of Azerbaijan, and Azerenergy OJSC, the country's electricity transmission system operator. In addition, Isayev highlighted the potential of grid-forming inverters, which provide additional flexibility and help improve power grid stability. He also spoke about the possible use of microgrids in industrial parks being established across various regions of Azerbaijan, particularly in areas where connecting to the main power grid is challenging. According to Isayev, microgrids could represent the next stage in the development of energy infrastructure, ensuring energy independence for industrial zones and residential areas.

artigo.texto: GS Engineering & Construction said Monday it had partnered with LS Electric, LG Uplus and Honeywell Technologies to shorten data center construction timelines amid growing demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure. The four companies signed a memorandum of understanding at the Grand InterContinental Seoul Parnas in southern Seoul to establish an integrated engineering framework covering four stages of development — procurement planning, design, system installation and integrated commissioning. The companies aim to agree on technical requirements early in each project to minimize design changes, duplicate work and delays between phases. That would help bring forward the ready-for-service date, when a data center can begin serving customers. GS E&C will coordinate technical work during system installation and provide engineering support for construction. LS Electric will review power systems and major equipment specifications and provide technical support for electrical infrastructure during integrated commissioning. Honeywell Technologies will contribute expertise in building automation, integrated controls, security and safety. The company plans to use its Forge industrial AI platform to help improve energy efficiency and operational reliability. Drawing on its experience operating large-scale data centers, LG Uplus will help define customer requirements and set criteria for operating and accepting completed facilities. It will also help validate operating procedures for emergencies such as power outages. The companies plan to hold regular working-level meetings to define responsibilities and work out how to apply the framework to future data center projects. The agreement follows GS E&C’s recent partnerships on data center power infrastructure, prefabricated modular data centers and immersion cooling technology. GS E&C said delivering projects quickly is becoming increasingly important as demand for AI data centers grows. yejinlim@heraldcorp.com

artigo.texto: New York Data Centers - Manhattan’s 60 Hudson Street and 111 Eighth Avenue (now Google-owned) are among the most interconnected buildings on Earth — critical nodes for global internet traffic. - ConEdison rates of 20–25¢/kWh make NYC the most expensive data center market in the country, while upstate utilities offer 6–8¢/kWh near Niagara Falls hydropower. - A 2022–2024 moratorium on fossil-fueled crypto mining reshaped the upstate pipeline without affecting traditional data centers. Manhattan Carrier Hotels to Hudson Valley Campuses New York’s data center geography reflects a stark economic divide. Lower Manhattan hosts iconic carrier hotels — 60 Hudson Street and 111 Eighth Avenue — where financial institutions pay premium rates for sub-millisecond latency to Wall Street. The Hudson Valley has emerged as a lower-cost alternative, with operators in Westchester and Orange counties building campuses that maintain fiber links to NYC at a fraction of Manhattan real estate costs. Upstate New York attracts operators seeking cheap hydroelectric power near Niagara Falls and Syracuse, though the 2022–2024 moratorium on fossil-fueled crypto mining reshuffled some of that pipeline. New York’s Data Center Counties 26 New York counties have tracked facilities, spanning from dense urban colocation in Manhattan to hyperscale builds along the I-87 corridor. The split mirrors the state’s broader economic geography: downstate pays for proximity and connectivity; upstate competes on cost and clean energy. Wall Street, Big Tech, and the Latency Premium New York’s operator mix is unlike any other market. Financial institutions drive demand in Manhattan and northern New Jersey, paying enormous premiums for microseconds of latency advantage. Equinix, Digital Realty, and Sabey Data Centers provide the colocation infrastructure. Google’s ownership of the iconic 111 Eighth Avenue symbolizes big tech’s presence, while the Hudson Valley attracts operators like EdgeConneX and Stack Infrastructure building for NYC-adjacent demand at lower cost. New York’s Highest-Capacity Facilities Genesee County tops the capacity ranking at 1,500 MW. The largest New York facilities are no longer in Manhattan — space and power constraints have pushed hyperscale capacity to the Hudson Valley and upstate, where land is available and utility rates can be one-fifth of ConEdison’s. Climate Mandates and a Bifurcated Pipeline New York’s pipeline reflects the state’s Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act (CLCPA), which requires 70% renewable electricity by 2030. Operators are shifting toward renewable energy procurement and behind-the-meter generation to comply. The pipeline is bifurcated: high-value, low-latency colocation in NYC proper, and hyperscale campuses in the Hudson Valley and upstate. The 13 facilities in development are weighted toward the latter. ConEdison vs. Upstate: A 4x Rate Differential No state has a wider electricity price gap within its borders. ConEdison in NYC charges commercial customers 20–25¢/kWh — the highest rates of any major data center market. Upstate utilities like National Grid and NYSEG charge closer to 6–8¢/kWh, and facilities near Niagara Falls access even cheaper hydroelectric power. This price gradient explains the ongoing migration of price-sensitive workloads upstate, while latency-critical financial applications remain tethered to Manhattan. The NYISO market allows large consumers to hedge costs through forward contracts. Compare current New York electricity rates across utility territories. Frequently Asked Questions Why is Manhattan a data center hub despite extreme costs? Manhattan’s data center market exists because of latency requirements. Financial institutions on Wall Street, media companies, and ad-tech firms need sub-millisecond connectivity to exchanges, content delivery networks, and each other. Carrier hotels like 60 Hudson Street and 111 Eighth Avenue are among the most interconnected buildings in the world. For these customers, the premium of 20–25¢/kWh electricity is justified by the value of proximity. What happened with New York's crypto mining moratorium? In November 2022, New York enacted a two-year moratorium on new fossil-fueled proof-of-work cryptocurrency mining operations (S6486D). The law, which expired in 2024, did not affect existing operations or renewable-powered mining. It did not apply to traditional data centers or cloud computing facilities. On July 14, 2026, Governor Hochul signed Executive Order 62, pausing state environmental permits for data centers over 50 MW until a generic environmental impact statement is completed. How expensive is electricity for New York data centers? Costs vary dramatically by location. ConEdison in NYC charges commercial customers 20–25¢/kWh, among the highest in the nation. Upstate utilities like National Grid and NYSEG charge closer to 6–8¢/kWh, and facilities near Niagara Falls can access even cheaper hydroelectric power. What submarine cables connect to New York? New York and New Jersey host multiple transatlantic submarine cable landing stations connecting to Europe. These cables land at stations in Long Island and northern New Jersey, with backhaul fiber running to Manhattan carrier hotels, making NYC a critical node for international internet traffic. How many data centers are in New York? New York has 199 tracked data center facilities across 26 counties. Facilities range from dense colocation hubs in Manhattan to hyperscale campuses in the Hudson Valley and upstate. Which companies operate the most data centers in New York? Major operators include Equinix, Digital Realty, DataBank, Sabey Data Centers, CyrusOne, and QTS. Google owns the iconic 111 Eighth Avenue building. In the Hudson Valley, EdgeConneX and Stack Infrastructure are building hyperscale campuses.

artigo.texto: Virginia Data Centers - Loudoun County alone hosts more data centers than most entire states — making Virginia the largest data center market in the world. - Data centers consume roughly 28% of Virginia’s total electricity, a higher share than any other U.S. state. Dominion Energy projects this load could double by 2030. - 176 facilities are in the pipeline as operators push beyond Northern Virginia into Prince William, Henrico, and Fauquier counties. Northern Virginia’s Data Center Alley The term “Data Center Alley” refers to the dense cluster of campuses along the Loudoun County Technology Corridor, centered on Ashburn. This corridor exists because of MAE-East, one of the original internet exchange points established in the early 1990s near Dulles Airport. Once carriers co-located there, network effects made the location self-reinforcing — today, roughly 70% of the world’s internet traffic passes through Northern Virginia daily. Growth is now spilling south into Prince William County and west toward Fauquier County, while Henrico County near Richmond has emerged as a secondary hub with lower land costs and direct fiber routes to coastal submarine cable landings. Every County with a Data Center in Virginia 30 Virginia counties have at least one tracked data center. Loudoun County dominates with 231 facilities, but the geographic footprint is expanding — Culpeper, Spotsylvania, and Fauquier counties have all seen new development since 2024. Amazon, Microsoft, and the Race for Northern Virginia Amazon Web Services alone operates dozens of facilities across Northern Virginia, making it both the largest operator and the largest electricity consumer in the region. Microsoft and Google are close behind, each investing billions in multi-building campuses. The colocation market is anchored by Equinix, QTS (Blackstone), Digital Realty, and CloudHQ, which lease space to hundreds of enterprise tenants. Virginia’s Highest-Capacity Facilities Several Virginia projects exceed 1 GW of planned capacity — each rivaling the output of a nuclear reactor. The scale reflects the shift from traditional colocation to hyperscale AI training, where a single building can draw more power than a small city. Loudoun County leads with 4,610 MW of tracked capacity. Moratorium Debates Haven’t Slowed Virginia’s Pipeline Despite vocal opposition in Loudoun and Prince William counties — where residents cite noise, aesthetics, and grid strain — Virginia’s construction pipeline remains the largest in the nation. Amazon, Microsoft, and Google each have multi-billion-dollar campus expansions underway. Dominion Energy has committed over $2 billion in dedicated transmission infrastructure to serve the corridor, and the utility recently created a dedicated rate class (GS-5) for data center customers drawing more than 25 MW. See our moratorium tracker for the latest restrictions. Dominion Energy, Data Centers, and Your Electric Bill Virginia’s data center boom has triggered billions in Dominion Energy transmission upgrades whose costs flow into regulated rates. The utility has proposed dedicated data center tariffs to insulate residential customers, but critics argue that existing cost allocation already spreads infrastructure expenses across all ratepayers. Virginia’s JLARC study found data centers are currently paying their fair share but warned that could change without structural reforms. Industrial electricity in NoVA averages 7–8¢/kWh. It is the largest concentration of data centers in the world, originally anchored by MAE-East, one of the first major internet exchange points established in the early 1990s. Today, over 518 facilities operate across Virginia, with Loudoun County alone hosting more data centers than most entire states. Why is Northern Virginia the data center capital of the world? Three factors created NoVA’s dominance: network density (fiber routes from MAE-East and multiple submarine cable connections), proximity to federal agencies and the Pentagon, and Dominion Energy’s reliable grid infrastructure. Once the first carriers co-located in Ashburn, network effects made the corridor self-reinforcing — every new facility adds peering value for all others. Are there data center moratoriums in Virginia? Several Northern Virginia jurisdictions have considered or enacted temporary restrictions. Loudoun County has debated zoning limits on data center expansion near residential areas, and Prince William County imposed a temporary moratorium in some zones in 2022. Loudoun County ended by-right approval for data centers in 2025. On September 18, 2026, Governor Spanberger signed Executive Order 22, ending by-right approval for facilities over 25 MW statewide and imposing water, noise, and cost-shift rules. These measures aim to balance economic growth with concerns about noise, aesthetics, and grid strain. See our moratorium tracker for current status. How much electricity do Virginia data centers consume? Virginia data centers consume an estimated 32 TWh annually — roughly 28% of the state’s total electricity demand, the highest share of any U.S. state. Dominion Energy projects data center load in its service territory could double by 2030, requiring billions in generation and transmission investment. Which companies have the most data centers in Virginia? artigo.texto: Em meio à onda de protestos contra o alto custo de vida e políticas armamentistas na Europa e na Itália, uma nova causa reuniu centenas de pessoas em Milão, neste sábado (21), contrárias à construção de data centers na região. Os manifestantes, que partiram da Piazza Repubblica em direção ao Palazzo Lombardia, sede do governo regional, citaram um estudo da Universidade de Cambridge que sugere que a construção de data centers pode elevar a temperatura em vários graus, mesmo a quilômetros de distância. Eles também apontaram a questão do ruído — um zumbido constante e ininterrupto na área de implantação — como outra possível ameaça ao meio ambiente e à saúde pública. Os ativistas também destacaram um posicionamento recente do Instituto Superior de Saúde da Itália, que emitiu um parecer negativo em relação à instalação de um data center em Lacchiarella, região metropolitana de Milão. "Como um município pode conceder a conformidade urbanística antes que uma 'avaliação de impacto à saúde' ou uma 'avaliação de impacto ambiental' tenha sido realizada?", questionaram os participantes do protesto. "Sabe por que isso acontece? Porque as forças de mercado são priorizadas em detrimento de um planejamento sério, que leve em conta todas as possíveis consequências e os requisitos de compatibilidade necessários", afirmou o Comitê Ciarlasco, movimento popular de Lacchiarella contra a implantação de data centers. "Privilegiar as forças de mercado em vez de um planejamento rigoroso abre caminho para uma 'colonização digital', uma vez que se permite que o mercado tenha precedência sobre a proteção da saúde pública", frisou o Comitê. A eurodeputada Ilaria Salis, da Aliança Verdes e Esquerda (AVS), participou da passeata neste sábado. "Estamos aqui porque a Lombardia é uma das regiões mais afetadas [da Itália] pelo desenvolvimento de data centers", explicou Salis, antes de acrescentar: "A questão é que essa concentração [de data centers] traz riscos ao meio ambiente e à saúde dos cidadãos". artigo.texto: Comment: UK-EU ETS Linkage A comment on the expected announcement that the UK and the EU are set to link their emissions trading schemes (ETS's) By Tom Cantillon info@eciu.net Share Last updated: Tom Cantillon, Senior Analyst at the Energy and Climate intelligence Unit (ECIU) said, "A range of industry associations support linking our carbon market with the EU’s, because it will strengthen and stabilise the market [1]. Strong carbon markets are vital if we want to futureproof our industries and protect them from losing out to cheaper, dirtier competitors. Not only that, linking the systems will improve market access for our exports to the EU, as products like steel and electricity will no longer face an EU carbon border tariff. This means all the revenue from carbon pricing will stay in the UK, to be spent by governments here, instead of those taxes ending up in EU coffers [2]. “Combined with the UK’s carbon border tariff to be introduced in January [3], this move will also protect UK industries from being undercut by cheap, dirty imports that come from outside the EU, such as Chinese steel. “Emissions trading schemes are increasingly the norm – with 30% of global emissions covered by a carbon price of some kind, and established schemes in countries like Canada, South Korea, China, South Africa and Vietnam [4]. When you poll the public, they overwhelmingly back the principle of making high-polluting industries pay tax on the emissions they produce – carbon markets and border tariffs uphold that principle, while financially incentivising companies to reduce their emissions over time [5].” Explainer: ETS, CBAM and fertiliser ETS linkage has long been supported by industry associations like Energy UK, UK Steel and the Mineral Products Association, on the basis that it will lead to a larger more liquid carbon market, reduce price instability, and boost investor confidence. They also see it benefitting business via reduced transaction and administrative costs. Coupled with a well-functioning UK CBAM, it is seen as a means to protect British industry from carbon dumping while supporting decarbonisation. Analysts have also suggested that linkage will lead to lower carbon prices in the long-term versus an unlinked scenario, potentially 40% higher by the early 2030s. Energy costs are often discussed in the context of Britian’s industrial competitiveness, driven largely by gas prices, as industry is mostly exempt from policy and network costs. A specific debate in this context is the impact of ETS and CBAM on UK fertiliser, with concerns raise that these have a negative impact on UK farmers via increased fertiliser costs. The evidence suggests that this will not be the case, if it does occur, for several years. This is for three primary reasons: Gas sets the price of fertiliser. Ammonium nitrate (AN), the UK’s main nitrogen fertiliser, is made from natural gas. ECIU analysis of AHDB fertiliser price data [6] and UK gas prices shows that the gas price has been on average more than a quarter of fertilisers’ price since 2017, and around three-fifths at the height of the energy crisis. The UK CBAM adds little to cost in the short term. When the UK CBAM enters into force in 2027, it will add an estimated £4 per tonne for non-EU imported AN against a price of £470/t for AN. That is equivalent to an ordinary month’s fluctuation in fertiliser prices, or the effect on production costs of a normal, single-day move in the gas price [7]. Most of our fertiliser comes from Europe, and linkage exempts it. Around three-fifths of the UK’s nitrogen fertiliser imports come from the EU, and virtually all imported AN [8]. With linked carbon markets, the groundwork is laid for an exemption of these imports from UK CBAM, meaning their cost-impact is avoided. CBAM levies are expected to rise year-on-year as free allocation of allowances are phased out. This is set out years in advance and can be planned for. The primary risk to farmers’ fertiliser bill is another gas price spike. Nitrogen fertiliser prices roughly tripled during the gas crisis and remain around double pre-crisis levels [9]. ENDS Notes to editors: [1] See statements from Energy UK, UK Steel and the Mineral Products Association [4] https://carbonpricingdashboard.worldbank.org [5] https://climatebarometer.org/as-climate-impacts-intensify-who-should-pay-for-the-costs/ [6] https://ahdb.org.uk/GB-fertiliser-prices [7] HMRC’s illustrative 2027 CBAM levy for fertiliser is £1.45/tCO2e. Applied to the EU’s default value for imported AN (2.0-2.7 tCO2e/t) this is around £3-4/t. The median monthly price swing for imported fertiliser, over the past two years based on AHDB data, is roughly £6/t. Making a tonne of ammonium nitrate uses about 13 GJ of gas, roughly 127 therms. So every 1p/therm change in the gas price changes the cost of a tonne by about £1.30, and 10p/therm by about £13. On that basis, the £3–4/t carbon border charge is equivalent to a move of about 2.5–3p/therm in the daily gas price, a swing regularly experienced in the market. [8] Based on UK Trade Data of fertiliser commodities in-scope for UK CBAM. [9] Based on AHDB fertiliser price data: AN (UK/imported) 3.5/3.8x during gas crisis, now 2.0/2.1x; Urea 3.4x at peak, now 1.8x; UAN 3.3x at peak now 1.9x; DAP/TSP 3.2x at peak now 2.2x

artigo.texto: Brasil mira boom de data centers até 2030 O Brasil se prepara para um crescimento expressivo no setor de data centers até 2030, conforme apontam projeções do mercado. O país busca converter sua matriz energética limpa e a crescente demanda digital em uma vantagem competitiva regional. O movimento ocorre em um contexto global de aceleração da digitalização e da necessidade de infraestrutura de processamento de dados. No interior paulista, o maior data center da América Latina já opera em Vinhedo, um modesto complexo de 61 megawatts (MW). A unidade serve como referência para o potencial de expansão do setor no território nacional. Empresários e gestores públicos observam com atenção os desdobramentos dessa tendência para a economia local. Infraestrutura silenciosa e operação contínua O monólito cinzento é silencioso por dentro. Máquinas zumbem, o ar frio circula e técnicos deslizam pelos corredores como fantasmas. A descrição, presente em relatos sobre a instalação de Vinhedo, ilustra o ambiente controlado e a rotina discreta desses centros de processamento. A operação exige precisão e monitoramento constante, características que demandam mão de obra qualificada. Do lado de fora do maior data center da América Latina, a estrutura aparenta simplicidade, mas abriga sistemas complexos de armazenamento e transmissão de dados. A fonte não detalhou os investimentos específicos em expansão, mas o setor projeta crescimento contínuo até o fim da década. Esse cenário tende a gerar oportunidades para fornecedores de serviços e equipamentos na região. Energia limpa como diferencial competitivo A região tenta converter energia limpa e demanda digital em vantagem competitiva. O Brasil possui uma das matrizes elétricas mais renováveis do mundo, o que atrai empresas globais de tecnologia que buscam reduzir emissões de carbono. Data centers consomem grandes volumes de energia, e a disponibilidade de fontes limpas é um fator decisivo para novos investimentos. Para o noroeste paulista, a expansão do setor pode gerar demanda por serviços de manutenção, segurança e logística. Pequenas e médias empresas de Araçatuba, Birigui e Penápolis podem se beneficiar indiretamente, fornecendo insumos ou mão de obra terceirizada. A fonte não detalhou projeções de empregos diretos, mas o histórico do setor indica efeito multiplicador na economia local. Impacto no comércio e na indústria regional O avanço dos data centers no estado de São Paulo tende a aquecer o mercado imobiliário industrial e o setor de construção civil. Cidades próximas a grandes centros de processamento podem atrair empresas de suporte técnico e logística. A instalação de Vinhedo, por exemplo, já movimenta a economia da região metropolitana de Campinas, com reflexos em municípios vizinhos. Comerciantes de Araçatuba e região devem observar as cadeias de suprimentos que se formam ao redor desses empreendimentos. Fornecedores de materiais elétricos, refrigeração e segurança patrimonial podem encontrar novas oportunidades de negócio. A fonte não detalhou valores de investimento, mas o crescimento projetado até 2030 sugere demanda consistente por serviços especializados. Perspectivas para a próxima década O Brasil mira boom de data centers até 2030, com potencial para se tornar um hub regional de processamento de dados. A combinação de energia renovável, estabilidade institucional e mercado consumidor amplo favorece a atração de capital estrangeiro. Especialistas ouvidos pela reportagem não forneceram números específicos, mas o tom é de otimismo moderado. Para o empresariado do interior paulista, a recomendação é acompanhar editais e licitações de infraestrutura digital. Entidades como ACSP, CDL e Sebrae podem oferecer capacitação para pequenos negócios que desejam se inserir nessa cadeia produtiva. A fonte não detalhou políticas públicas específicas, mas o setor privado já sinaliza interesse em expandir operações no estado. A transição para uma economia mais digital exige planejamento e adaptação por parte dos agentes locais. O exemplo de Vinhedo demonstra que mesmo estruturas aparentemente isoladas geram empregos e renda em seu entorno. Até 2030, o Brasil pode consolidar sua posição como destino estratégico para data centers na América Latina. O maior data center da América Latina, localizado em Vinhedo (SP), tem capacidade de 61 megawatts (MW). Como o Brasil pretende usar energia limpa para impulsionar o setor de data centers até 2030?
