artigo.texto: - Link intended to be operational from January 1, 2028, with UK and EU allowances valid in either scheme - UK ETS to cover 50% of international voyage emissions from the same date - UK auction reserve price scrapped when the link goes live - Northern Ireland derogation goes, island ro-pax and ice-class derogations kept to end-2030 The UK and EU have agreed to link their emissions trading systems, with the link intended to be operational from January 1, 2028, the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero said in an explainer published on Friday. From that date allowances issued under either scheme can be used for compliance in the other, including for 2027 emissions, with the first joint surrender deadline on September 30, 2028. Operators should also be able to use one pool of allowances for both their UK and EU obligations, without needing to buy UK allowances (UKAs) and EU allowances (EUAs) separately, greatly simplifying compliance requirements for those on international voyages. For shipping, the agreement confirms that the UK Emissions Trading Scheme (UK ETS) will expand to cover 50% of emissions from international voyages by ships of 5,000 GT and above from the same date, alongside the 100% of domestic and in-port emissions it has covered since July 1, 2026. The expansion was first set out last November with the same January 1, 2028 start, so the UK's coverage of international shipping and the allowance link now begin together. The EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) already covers 50% of emissions on voyages between an EU port and a port outside the bloc. As part of the move, the UK will remove its auction reserve price when the link goes live, since "it would not be practical or desirable to maintain a price floor in only one part of a linked market," the explainer says. UK allowances have traded below EUAs since the scheme began, and earlier this year Ship & Bunker calculated an average discount of 21.8% in the first half of 2026. Derogations The agreement removes the temporary 50% surrender derogation for voyages between Northern Ireland and Great Britain, "as planned", so that all covered Irish Sea voyages face the same 100% obligation. The UK will align with the EU's temporary derogation for passenger and ro-pax voyages to islands with fewer than 200,000 people and no road or rail link to the mainland, until at least December 31, 2030, and ice-class ships will get a 5% surrender derogation to the same date. Shipping companies will be able to apply a zero emission factor to biofuels, RFNBOs and recycled carbon fuels that meet the Renewable Energy Directive's criteria. Should a global measure be adopted at the IMO, the UK "will review its interactions with our own policy, to avoid any double charging of emissions", the document says. That said, the IBIA Annual Convention in New York heard last week that the EU is unlikely to give up the ETS whatever the outcome on the IMO Net-Zero Framework, with Peter Keller, Chairman of SEA-LNG, saying: "What government do we know anywhere in the world is prepared to give up tax revenue?" The deal came a day after the UK Chamber of Shipping called on both sides to use the reset talks to cut costs, asking for ETS revenues to support shipping's decarbonisation and for a full economic impact assessment before the UK ETS was extended internationally. "We also need to see the revenues raised from shipping support shipping's decarbonisation, rather than simply increasing ETS and compliance costs without delivering additional emissions reductions," a Chamber spokesperson said in a statement on Thursday. The explainer makes no mention of revenue for maritime decarbonisation.

artigo.texto: Scientists have long warned of the massively growing environmental footprint of AI data centers, facilities that are often powered by gas plants and releasing a staggering amount of pollution and waste heat. In an effort to maximize the amount of available solar energy — and avoid the wrath of a public that has squarely turned against data centers — tech CEOs have become increasingly serious about launching the facilities into orbit instead. SpaceX, in particular, has taken the concept to its extreme, with CEO Elon Musk proposing the launch of up to one million orbital data centers, each significantly larger than the International Space Station, to meet the surging demands for AI computing power. But besides some glaring questions surrounding the concept’s viability and the potentially debilitating effects for astronomy research, the orbiting satellites could multiply certain forms of pollution by over 100 times, University College London chemistry professor Eloise Marais and research fellow Connor Barker argue in a new paper to be published in the journal Earth and Space Chemistry. The team found that launching such a large number of data centers could boost total emissions from rocket launches, including the release of ozone-damaging chemicals and other pollutants into the upper atmosphere, by more than 150 times compared to last year’s measurements — while generating up to 150 times more nitrogen oxides released during reentry. While scientists have long suspected that SpaceX’s workhorse Falcon 9 rocket is releasing copious amounts of potentially ozone layer-damaging chemicals during launch, the company’s much larger Starship rocket could exacerbate the environmental damage considerably. According to Marais and Barker’s calculations, the company would need to launch at least 5,000 Starship rockets a year to fill out its planned constellation — a huge number compared to the mere 330 orbital rockets that launched last year globally. However, the researchers had to base their paper of some major assumptions. As Scientific American points out, SpaceX has yet to disclose some basic information needed to gauge the exact environmental footprint of its lofty plans. “It became apparent [early on in our research] that the kind of information that’s needed isn’t there,” Marais told the magazine. For one, how much nitrogen oxides will be released by SpaceX’s reusable Super Heavy booster itself remains unclear at best. We also don’t know what materials the company will use for its hardware, meaning that the researchers were unable to estimate the toll that metal pollution would take on the atmosphere. Therefore, the duo is calling on companies to disclose more information about their launches. “There’s nothing here that’s perfect, but there has to be a solution to go forward that can simultaneously respect the proprietary information while also demanding that we know what is being dumped in the atmosphere,” University of British Columbia space pollution expert Aaron Boley, who was not involved in the study, told SciAm. Nonetheless, by basing their calculations on previous estimates involving NASA’s Space Shuttles, the team still found that Starships could release as much in nitrogen oxide emissions a year as an entire European country. “The unprecedented increase in anthropogenic chemicals stands to modify stratospheric aerosols, deplete ozone, alter climate, perturb mesospheric nitrogen, and degrade air quality,” the researchers concluded in their paper. “These risks should incite regulators to demand provision of information needed to calculate emissions and enable environmental impact assessments.” More on orbital data centers: Anybody Who Thinks Orbital Data Centers are a Good Idea Is Suffering from AI Psychosis, Experts Argue

artigo.texto: Key Takeaways - The temporary injunction also bars BYD from producing the Ti7 in Hungary. It does not cover the UK market. - BYD said it designed the Ti7 independently and will appeal the ruling. A Dutch district court in The Hague ruled on Friday that BYD's (HKEX: 1211) Ti7 SUV infringes Jaguar Land Rover's (JLR) EU design rights for the Land Rover Defender and issued a temporary injunction barring BYD from selling the SUV in the European Union. The dispute concerns the Defender 110, which JLR introduced in September 2019. JLR registered the vehicle's exterior design in the EU in 2018. The Ti7, known as the Tai 7 in China, is a top seller for BYD's Fang Cheng Bao sub-brand. Cumulative global sales passed 200,000 units in July and 300,000 in October. The Defender is JLR's best-selling model line, with global sales of more than 100,000 units in 2025, Reuters reported on Saturday. BYD said in a statement that it designed the Ti7 independently and that the SUV infringes none of JLR's rights, according to Reuters. The company said it strongly disagrees with the ruling and will appeal. The court found that the Ti7 and the Defender 110 have nearly identical body proportions, side window profiles, signature panels behind the rear passenger doors and rounded wheel arch corners. Together, those features define the vehicle's overall appearance, the court said. The differences BYD identified were too minor to change that impression. The injunction takes effect 1 week after the judgment is formally served. It covers activities including importing, manufacturing, selling and delivering the Ti7 in the EU. It also bars BYD from building the SUV at its plant in Hungary. BYD has yet to launch the Ti7 in the EU. The company told the court it had no concrete plans to do so, but declined to rule out a future launch. The court capped total penalties for violating the injunction at €10 million. JLR brought the case after BYD announced plans to launch the Ti7 in the UK, seeking to block sales in both the UK and the EU. BYD opened UK pre-orders for the 7-seat Ti7 in July and said at the time that it expected deliveries to begin in January 2027. The court found that it lacked jurisdiction over BYD's UK subsidiary. It also found that JLR had failed to show that BYD's Dutch entities were involved in offering or promoting the Ti7 in the UK. The judge therefore rejected JLR's request for a UK injunction. Because the Ti7 had yet to enter the EU market, the court also denied JLR's requests for access to commercial documents, information on distribution channels. The ruling is provisional. JLR must bring a case on the merits within 6 months of the ruling or the injunction could lapse. The company said in a statement that it takes legal action when necessary to protect its intellectual property. The Tai 7 was launched in China in September 2025 as a plug-in hybrid SUV. Fang Cheng Bao added a battery-electric version in April 2026. Cumulative sales of the Tai 7 reached 309,456 units by the end of October 2026, according to data compiled by CnEVPost. BYD also introduced the SUV in Uzbekistan in October, launching a 5-seat, all-wheel-drive plug-in hybrid under the name BYD Ti 7.

artigo.texto: Key Takeaways - The top-spec Fang Cheng Bao Tai 9 features a foldable steering wheel, turning a concept BYD showcased at the 2019 Shanghai Auto Show into reality. - BYD said the feature is not only a parked rest solution, but also a technology reserve for future L3 and L4 autonomous driving built on steer-by-wire. The world's first mass-produced foldable steering wheel, featured on the Tai 9 flagship SUV from BYD's (HKEX: 1211) Fang Cheng Bao brand, traces its conceptual roots back 7 years to the 2019 Shanghai Auto Show. On April 16, 2019, BYD debuted the E-SEED GT concept car at the Shanghai Auto Show, showcasing for the first time a retractable steering wheel that could fold into the dashboard in autonomous driving mode — a design widely viewed as science fiction at the time. The BYD E-SEED GT concept car showcased a retractable steering wheel design in 2019: Seven years later, that concept has reached mass production on the Tai 9, which was launched on November 19. The SUV starts at 279,900 yuan ($41,700), with the top-spec variant priced at 329,900 yuan featuring the foldable smart cockpit. The feature sparked some skepticism on the Chinese internet over whether it is necessary following its release, though such doubts have been rare in overseas communities. In a statement shared with CnEVPost on Monday, BYD said the foldable smart cockpit is not only a solution for current parked rest needs, but also a forward-looking technology reserve for future L3 and L4 autonomous driving. Videos highlight the details of the BYD Fang Cheng Bao Tai 9's foldable steering wheel. The core prerequisite for a foldable steering wheel is eliminating the mechanical steering column in favor of steer-by-wire technology. Its mass production was also enabled by regulatory relaxation in China. On July 1, 2026, China's mandatory national standard GB 17675-2025 took effect, removing the requirement for a mechanical connection in steering systems. BYD was one of the drafting units of the standard. Built on BYD's in-house steer-by-wire technology, the steering wheel uses a 180-degree hinge and high-precision motors derived from embodied AI robots, supporting folding from 0 to 180 degrees and taking about 10 seconds to stow away. Once folded, it frees up about 25 centimeters of legroom for the driver, pairing with a seat that reclines to 165 degrees to meet needs such as resting while waiting for a charge or camping. In terms of operational boundaries, the steering wheel can only be folded when the vehicle is completely stopped and shifted into Park. It cannot be operated while driving, and must be fully unfolded and locked before the vehicle is allowed to move. The steer-by-wire system features 5 layers of redundancy across power supply, communication, sensing, control, and actuation, and the folding system has obtained ASIL-D functional safety certification, according to the company. BYD said the folding mechanism has completed 96,000 durability tests across extreme temperatures ranging from -30°C (-22°F) to 85°C (185°F), with a start-stop lifespan of 80,000 cycles, and that the airbag has passed deployment verification in both folded and unfolded states. Around the foldable smart cockpit, BYD has filed a cumulative 272 patents and is positioning this top-spec technology anchor as an interface for next-generation smart cockpits, the company said. ($1 = 6.7120 yuan)

artigo.texto: Washington wants America’s AI infrastructure to stay home. But Americans aren’t sure they want it next door, and companies are discovering that building at home is becoming increasingly difficult. The future of U.S. data center investment now depends on whether America can make home the easiest place to build, not just the most expensive place to leave. A Friday Warning With No Details On Friday, November 20, President Donald Trump issued a warning to American companies expanding data center infrastructure overseas. The message was blunt: build in the United States, or face a “tremendous tax.” “We’re not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country,” Trump said at the White House. “If they do that, they can. But we’re going to put a tremendous tax on them.” He framed the threat around China, arguing that overseas infrastructure could ultimately benefit America’s biggest strategic competitor. “China will take all of them,” he said, explaining why he would not allow data centers to go into other countries. The announcement sounded decisive. The policy behind it, however, remains unclear. Trump provided no tax rate, implementation timeline or legal mechanism, and acknowledged that he had not yet discussed the proposal with his own officials. Congress’s role in imposing a new federal tax also remains a significant question, because a president cannot create a federal tax by announcement alone. But the threat raises a question bigger than what Washington intends to do to companies building abroad: If America wants companies to build at home, is it making the United States more attractive, or simply threatening the alternatives? That is the central question for U.S. data center investment. Why Companies Look Beyond America Data centers are the factories of the AI economy. They house the computing capacity needed to train AI models, operate cloud services and process billions of requests. Their location matters because electricity, cooling, connectivity, land, permitting and proximity to customers determine how quickly and economically they can operate. That is why international expansion is not automatically a retreat from America. Companies build abroad to serve customers in regional markets, meet data residency requirements, reduce latency and secure favorable operating conditions. International infrastructure can strengthen an American company’s global business rather than surrender it. Finland illustrates the point. In September 2026, Google announced a €13 billion investment in Finnish digital infrastructure, its largest investment in Europe. The expansion builds on Finland’s existing data center presence and reflects the country’s energy and infrastructure advantages, including access to carbon-free electricity and a cold climate that can help reduce cooling requirements. Finland is not China. It is a U.S. ally competing for investment. Google’s decision should prompt Washington to examine what makes overseas markets attractive, not assume every foreign project weakens America. If U.S. data center investment is to stay in America, Washington must compete on the same terms: power, price, speed and permission. What Americans Actually Want Here is the contradiction Washington cannot ignore: the government wants more data centers built at home, but many Americans do not want them in their communities. A Reuters/Ipsos poll published on June 11, 2026, surveying 4,531 people over six days, found that just 33 percent agreed it was mainly a good thing to build data centers at a rapid pace, while 64 percent disagreed. Some 57 percent said they would oppose a data center being built in their own community, including two-thirds of Democrats and half of Republicans. That finding has hardened, not softened. In a Gallup survey conducted March 2-18, 2026, among 1,000 U.S. adults, 71 percent opposed constructing an AI data center in their local area, including 48 percent who were strongly opposed. In the same survey, only 53 percent opposed a nuclear energy plant nearby, meaning data centers are now less popular than nuclear plants. By August 2026, the University of Pennsylvania’s Annenberg Public Policy Center reported that 61 percent of Americans opposed new data centers in their area, up from 49 percent earlier in the year. Opposition crossed party lines, with majorities of Democrats, Republicans and independents expressing resistance. An Ipsos Consumer Tracker released September 15, 2026, found 69 percent were concerned about the growth of AI data center construction in the United States, including 37 percent who were very concerned. Among those concerned, the top worries were strain on local water supplies at 50 percent, strain on the electrical grid at 41 percent, and higher residential utility bills at 35 percent. These are not simply objections to technology. Residents worry about who pays for grid upgrades, whether electricity bills will rise, how much water facilities consume, and whether communities have any meaningful say over projects that could reshape their surroundings. Washington wants America to host the AI boom. But the people expected to host the infrastructure are increasingly asking what they get in return. That question will decide the future of U.S. data center investment far more than any threat. The America That Says No The resistance is already affecting development. Data Center Watch reported that at least 75 U.S. projects valued at approximately $130 billion were blocked or delayed during the first quarter of 2026. In the second quarter, it recorded at least 45 additional project disruptions valued at nearly $68 billion. These are quarterly figures, not necessarily unique projects across the six-month period, but they show the scale of disruption. artigo.texto: Veja o resumo da notícia O Brasil busca ampliar sua participação no mercado global de data centers, impulsionado pelo crescimento da inteligência artificial (IA) e pela demanda por infraestrutura de processamento de dados. Segundo reportagem da revista britânica The Economist, o país reúne condições favoráveis para atrair investimentos no setor. Sendo assim, entre os principais diferenciais estão a oferta de energia renovável, o crescimento do mercado digital e a localização estratégica para conexões internacionais. Além disso, o avanço da inteligência artificial tem elevado a necessidade de capacidade computacional em diferentes regiões do mundo. Nesse cenário, o Brasil tenta se consolidar como um dos principais destinos para novos empreendimentos. Brasil atrai investimentos bilionários em data centers A expansão do setor já aparece em projetos anunciados no país. Em Vinhedo, no interior de São Paulo, a Ascenty desenvolve um complexo de data centers e planeja ampliar suas operações. De acordo com a The Economist, a companhia pretende investir US$ 1,2 bilhão na região, acompanhando o crescimento da demanda por armazenamento e processamento de dados. Desse modo, o movimento reflete o interesse de empresas em ampliar a infraestrutura necessária para sustentar serviços digitais e aplicações de inteligência artificial. Capacidade de data centers pode chegar a 5 GW até 2030 Apesar do potencial de crescimento, a América Latina ainda representa uma parcela pequena da infraestrutura mundial de data centers. Segundo a publicação britânica, a região possui menos de 600 instalações, com capacidade conjunta próxima de 1,5 gigawatt (GW). O volume é inferior ao registrado apenas no Reino Unido. O Brasil, por sua vez, concentra quase metade dessa capacidade, com aproximadamente 700 megawatts (MW) instalados. A expectativa é de expansão nos próximos anos. Alessandro Lombardi, presidente da Elea Data Centers, estima que a capacidade brasileira possa alcançar 5 GW até 2030. Caso a projeção se confirme, o país poderá ampliar significativamente sua presença no mercado internacional de infraestrutura digital, em meio à crescente demanda por processamento de dados e inteligência artificial.

artigo.texto: President Donald Trump has threatened to penalize US technology companies that build data centers overseas, saying they must keep their investments in the United States or face a “tremendous tax” during a White House press conference on November 20. Trump declared that companies could still build facilities abroad but would face additional taxes and he also acknowledged that he had not informed his staff about the proposal before announcing it. The proposal could affect major US technology companies, including Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle, which have invested in data centers overseas. These facilities allow cloud service providers to operate closer to international customers and comply with local data regulations. “We’re not going to allow our companies to build data centres outside of our country, I don’t know if that’s a breaking story, but I haven’t even said that to my people. But I’m telling them now, they’re here.” Trump told reporters at the White House after returning from his trip to Asia as reported by NBC News. “We’re not going to allow that to happen. You know, they allowed that to happen with chips and everything else, and it was very destructive to our country, we’re going to put tremendous penalties on companies that try and do it,” He added that the U.S. would tax any company that attempted to build a data center abroad but He did not explain how the proposed restrictions would be enforced or when they might take effect. Trump argued that restricting overseas construction would help the United States maintain its lead over China in artificial intelligence. His remarks followed a separate US policy announced earlier this week requiring licenses for purchases of advanced computer chips. The measure is intended to help authorities monitor where the chips are used and prevent computing resources from reaching Chinese companies as reported by CNBC. The proposed restrictions also come as data center construction faces growing opposition in the United States. A CNBC survey found that 64 percent of registered voters opposed having an AI data center within 10 miles of their homes, while only 13 percent supported one. Concerns include rising electricity demand, noise pollution and the impact of large facilities on nearby communities. Opposition to data center projects also became an issue in the November 3 midterm elections, with Democratic candidates campaigning for tighter construction regulations. The Pew Research Center estimated that the United States had about 3,000 data centers as of April, with another 1,500 in various stages of approval and construction. According to a report by the BBC, Canada has been positioning itself as an alternative location for major technology companies looking to expand their AI infrastructure. Trump urged communities to accept the projects and negotiate financial benefits rather than oppose them. “You ought to take advantage of the data centres. Make them pay you, make them pay your community, but take advantage don’t shut them off,” he said. No details have been provided on whether the proposed tax would apply to existing overseas facilities, future construction projects or both. It is also unclear whether the administration intends to introduce a formal ban or use tax penalties to discourage companies from investing abroad.

artigo.texto: South Korea Overtakes Japan in Solid-State Battery Patents South Korea led solid-state battery patent filings in 2024 as worldwide filings reached a record 2,230. Updated on Nov. 20, 2026 in Energy In 2024, South Korea overtook Japan as the leading source of solid-state battery patent filings, with 873 priority filings compared with Japan's 605. Worldwide solid-state battery priority filings rose 16% from 1,928 in 2023 to 2,230 in 2024. Why it matters Japan had led the solid-state category in every year up to 2023, so the shift marks a change in which country is building the strongest patent position in a technology seen as a potential successor to conventional lithium batteries. Filings for conventional lithium battery technology fell almost 15% to 2,092 over the same year, suggesting that inventive effort is moving toward solid-state designs. Priority filings, the first patent application for a given invention, were used to avoid counting the same invention across multiple jurisdictions. Samsung SDI raised its solid-state filings from 165 to 325 in one year, while Toyota recorded 144 and China 217, and European organisations recorded 177, a new high. The players Samsung SDI Samsung SDI is a South Korean battery manufacturer and affiliate of the Samsung group that supplies batteries for electric vehicles and energy storage. Toyota Toyota is a Japanese automaker that has pursued solid-state battery development for future electric vehicles. QuantumScape QuantumScape is a United States company developing solid-state lithium-metal battery technology for electric vehicles. The details The figures count priority filings, the first patent application made for a particular invention, which avoids double counting the same invention across jurisdictions. Samsung SDI more than doubled its solid-state filings in a single year, and European organisations reached a record 177 filings in 2024. Timeline - 2023: Japan led solid-state battery filings, with a worldwide baseline of 1,928 priority filings. - 2024: Worldwide solid-state filings reached a record 2,230, and South Korea overtook Japan. - 2020 to 2024: South Korean lithium-ion battery filings rose from 441 to 833. The Big Picture The 15% drop in conventional lithium battery filings to 2,092 in 2024, set against a 16% rise in solid-state filings, shows inventive effort shifting away from the lithium-ion designs that have dominated battery patenting. South Korea's rise past Japan indicates that the lead in solid-state patents is moving between national industries. Solid-state batteries are a candidate for future electric vehicles and energy storage, so the patent race shapes which manufacturers may later supply those products. The filings do not confirm when or whether these designs will reach consumers. The takeaway Patent filing trends can signal where future battery supply may come from, but filings alone do not confirm commercial success. Readers tracking electric vehicle or energy storage technology may watch whether filing growth translates into production. Further reading For more on the technologies behind this shift, explore the Energy section.

artigo.texto: No último dia 6, nove ONGs (entre as quais o Greenpeace) lançaram a campanha “Parem os mega data centers”, que me deixou curioso para entender o que as movia. No site da campanha, os argumentos são quatro: grandes data centers no Brasil podem encarecer a conta de luz, agravar a falta d’água, produzir um barulho “adoecedor” e aumentar as emissões de gases poluentes. Já aviso que a coluna de hoje é mais longa que o habitual, pois cada argumento merece uma análise. Vem comigo. 1. O barulho Para ilustrar este ponto, a campanha usou uma gravação acompanhada da frase “imagine esse som bem mais alto dia e noite na sua casa”. Mas que som é esse? O chiado agudo do vídeo vem dos equipamentos que jogam o calor para fora do prédio: chillers (centrais de refrigeração com compressores e baterias de ventiladores), torres de resfriamento e dry coolers, instalados no telhado ou no pátio. E há vários casos de comunidades americanas expostas a esse ruído e movendo processos, como contra a Microsoft, em Wisconsin, e contra a Hyperscale Data, em Michigan. Este data center de Michigan nasceu como mineradora de bitcoin, que costuma fazer trocas de ar com o exterior por ventiladores, sem isolamento. Com aberturas para o ar circular, o som escapa. Um outro ruído possível é o dos geradores. Com o gás natural barato, vários data centers americanos foram projetados para rodar fora da rede nos primeiros anos, com termelétricas próprias. Se o gerador for uma turbina a gás natural, o som lembra o de um avião a jato taxiando. Em geradores a diesel, o som é mais grave (como se ouve neste vídeo, com 14 gigantescos Perkins V12 ligados ao mesmo tempo). Os geradores a diesel servem de reserva para quedas de energia, mas não para geração contínua: nos EUA, o MWh gerado a diesel custa de 2 a 3 vezes mais. Ambos são desagradáveis, mas bem diferentes do ruído de alta frequência da peça publicitária. E aqui no Brasil? Fui checar pessoalmente, diante de um dos maiores data centers do País, em Barueri, junto ao Rodoanel. Desliguei o redutor de ruído do microfone para captar todo o som ambiente. O único som que chama a atenção é o do trânsito. Não há nada parecido com o chiado do anúncio, nem o ronco grave de geradores. O motivo: em clima quente e úmido como o nosso, o resfriamento líquido em circuito fechado é praticamente mandatório. E a autogeração contínua, mesmo com gás natural, é economicamente inviável aqui. Além disso, diferente dos EUA, no Brasil temos uma norma nacional para emissão de ruídos. A NBR 10151, da ABNT, fixa como limites 50 decibéis de dia e 45 à noite em áreas estritamente residenciais. 2. A conta de luz Nos EUA, o efeito dos data centers nos preços de energia está bem documentado. Um estudo de pesquisadores da Universidade Cornell, publicado no último dia 9 na revista Nature Energy, analisou quatro grandes redes elétricas americanas entre 2020 e 2025. Em 2025, os data centers pagaram só 38% dos US$ 8,25 bilhões em obras de infraestrutura ligadas ao seu crescimento. Os outros 62% ficaram, em grande parte, com os consumidores residenciais. E o peso foi maior nas famílias rurais e de baixa renda. E no Brasil? Ainda é cedo para dizer. Segundo o especialista em infraestrutura de data centers Thiago Ayub, os mais de 250 data centers em operação no País não provocaram aumento na conta de luz. Mas ele reconhece que os novos centros de treinamento de inteligência artificial em fase de implantação são de outra escala. Por ora, o setor ainda é pequeno. Segundo a Brasscom, associação das empresas de tecnologia, os data centers consumiram 8,2 TWh em 2024, ou 1,7% da eletricidade do País. As residências, lembra Ayub, passam de 25%. Há também uma diferença estrutural. O Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN) permite gerar energia em um estado e consumi-la em outro. Nos EUA, redes como a do Texas operam quase isoladas e novos grandes consumidores têm maior impacto na vizinhança imediata. Mas no Brasil existe um risco de outra natureza: o tributário. O Redata, regime de incentivos fiscais sancionado em 15 de setembro, prevê renúncia de R$ 5,2 bilhões só em 2026. E aí temos um caso de cobertor curto: o que é descoberto por um lado precisa ser coberto por alguém. O Idec propôs um encargo específico para grandes consumidores, para que a expansão da rede não vá parar na conta dos demais. 3. A água Este me parece ser o argumento de maior impacto na percepção pública. Afinal, quanto consome um data center? Depende do sistema de resfriamento. Na torre evaporativa, de ciclo aberto, parte da água evapora o tempo todo e precisa ser reposta. É o sistema mais comum nos EUA. Já no circuito fechado, a água circula sem sair, como no radiador do carro: há um abastecimento inicial e pequenas reposições. Segundo Thiago Ayub, os grandes data centers em operação e em construção no Brasil usam esse sistema, e a torre evaporativa é raridade por aqui. Para pôr em perspectiva, vou considerar o campus da Scala em Tamboré, Barueri, que tem mais de 120 MW em operação. A Brasscom estima 23 mil litros por MW para encher o sistema, com reposição de cerca de 10% ao ano. Isto resulta em cerca de 2,8 milhões de litros, pouco mais que uma piscina olímpica (2,5 milhões) – lembrando que a reposição numa piscina olímpica (por evaporação e filtração) é bem maior. Em poucas palavras, um abastecimento inicial maior, com uma reposição (consumo) baixa. Quando este campus chegar aos 600 MW previstos, serão 13,8 milhões de litros para encher o sistema, ou cinco piscinas olímpicas e meia. Mas essa água fica no circuito. O consumo de fato é a reposição: 1,4 milhão de litros, equivalente à água de irrigação de 260 kg de amêndoas na Califórnia. Existe um projeto em andamento em Caucaia (CE) de um data center de 300 MW que pretende consumir 30 mil litros de água por dia quando em operação normal. Não consegui encontrar detalhamento do projeto que explique este fluxo diário (e não um abastecimento único) – mas, de qualquer maneira, isto equivale ao consumo médio diário residenc

artigo.texto: The European Union and the United Kingdom have reached agreements on youth mobility, food and animal-product trade, and linking their emissions trading systems, marking a step towards rebuilding relations nearly a decade after the Brexit referendum. The agreements were announced after a summit in Brussels on Friday. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s office said negotiations on the three areas had concluded, while a joint statement setting out further details is expected to be published. “This is a good day for Britain. This is a good day for Europe, and people across Europe and across the United Kingdom will get real benefit,” Burnham said at the start of talks with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa. The planned sanitary and phytosanitary agreement would reduce checks on animals, plants and related products moving between the UK and the EU. The arrangement is estimated to be worth £5.1 billion ($6.7 billion) to the British economy. The two sides have also agreed to link their emissions trading systems. The arrangement is intended to exempt British and EU goods, including steel, from each other’s border carbon levies. Under the proposed youth mobility scheme, up to 100,000 young people from each side would be able to live and work in the other jurisdiction for as long as three years. The governments have agreed on timelines for implementing the scheme, although further details have not yet been released. A UK government spokesperson told Al Jazeera that negotiations on the agreements had concluded and that both sides would now work towards implementation. The spokesperson said each country would follow its own legal process and that discussions would continue in other areas. Burnham said the agreements could add 0.5 percent to the UK economy. However, the deals represent only an initial stage in a broader effort to reset relations, with further negotiations expected to take months or, in some areas, years. Burnham has previously said that all options for the UK’s future relationship with Europe should remain open, including the possibility of rejoining the EU. He has also stressed that reversing Brexit is only one possible outcome and is not imminent. The agreements are likely to face criticism from eurosceptics in the UK. Nigel Farage, leader of the Reform UK party, called Burnham “naive” and accused the EU of trying to “strong-arm” the prime minister. In a social media post, Farage said it was “the same old game” and claimed Burnham had fallen for it through inexperience.

artigo.texto: Implementar uma transição verde, reduzir as emissões de carbono e abrir caminho para uma economia verde. Hai Phong está intensificando os esforços para reduzir as emissões de carbono, desenvolver um mercado de créditos de carbono e criar valor econômico e vantagens competitivas para as empresas. Para implementar a transformação verde, a cidade de Hai Phong concentra-se em soluções para desenvolver a capacidade de inventário e governança de carbono e participar do sistema de negociação de cotas de emissão de gases de efeito estufa; desenvolvendo um mercado de carbono, transformando os esforços de redução de emissões de carbono das empresas em valor econômico real. A respeito dessa solução, o jornal, rádio e televisão de Hai Phong dialogou com o camarada Bui Van Thang, membro do Comitê Permanente do Partido Comunista da Cidade e diretor do Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente – órgão permanente do Comitê Diretivo para a Transformação Verde da Cidade de Hai Phong. — Camarada, por que Hai Phong identificou a redução das emissões de carbono como uma das tarefas principais do plano de transformação verde da cidade? - A Resolução nº 08-NQ/TU do Comitê Permanente do Partido Comunista da Cidade de Hai Phong sobre a transformação verde da cidade de Hai Phong no período de 2026 a 2030, com uma visão para 2050, emitida em 29 de janeiro de 2026, define claramente a transformação verde como uma tarefa central e contínua; a economia circular como a força motriz; e o porto verde como um avanço estratégico. A redução das emissões de carbono é um objetivo fundamental, servindo como um passo importante para uma economia verde e uma medida direta do sucesso da transição verde. A meta é reduzir as emissões de gases de efeito estufa em pelo menos 43,5% em comparação com 2020, visando emissões líquidas zero até 2045. Isso inclui promover a adoção de padrões ESG (Ambientais, Sociais e de Governança), a economia circular e a realização de inventários de gases de efeito estufa nas empresas. A determinação de Hai Phong será medida não apenas pelo montante de investimento planejado ou pelo número de projetos aprovados, mas também pela quantidade de toneladas de emissões reduzidas. Quando esses indicadores forem divulgados publicamente e de forma transparente, os cidadãos terão uma base para monitorar a qualidade ambiental; as empresas terão dados para otimizar suas operações; e os órgãos de gestão terão uma base precisa para avaliar o progresso e alocar recursos. Nesse ponto, a "transformação verde" deixaria de ser um slogan e se tornaria uma capacidade de desenvolvimento inerente e uma nova vantagem competitiva para Hai Phong. Somente quando a transformação verde se tornar um padrão obrigatório na seleção de investimentos, na operação portuária, na organização da produção industrial, no desenvolvimento urbano, na gestão do turismo e nos hábitos de vida da comunidade, a Resolução nº 08-NQ/TU será verdadeiramente implementada de forma sólida e duradoura. Identificar claramente soluções para a redução de emissões contribuirá para melhorar a eficiência dos recursos, promover o uso de energia limpa, desenvolver tecnologias verdes e aumentar a capacidade de adaptação às mudanças climáticas. Essa solução é crucial no contexto do desenvolvimento acelerado da indústria, das áreas urbanas, da logística e de outros setores econômicos com altos níveis de emissão em Hai Phong. - De que forma Hai Phong lançou as bases e implementou os primeiros passos em seu roteiro de redução de emissões de carbono? O período de 2026 a 2030 é considerado crucial para Hai Phong concretizar suas diretrizes de transformação verde, redução das emissões de gases de efeito estufa e utilização eficiente dos recursos. Reconhecendo que as empresas manufatureiras são os principais atores na redução das emissões, o plano de redução de emissões de CO2 da cidade vai além do simples estabelecimento de metas; ele visa desenvolver programas e tarefas viáveis, adaptados a cada indústria, setor e área de desenvolvimento da cidade. A cidade possui 110 instalações na lista daquelas obrigadas a realizar inventários de gases de efeito estufa, incluindo 89 no setor industrial e comercial, 19 no setor de construção e transporte e 2 no setor agrícola e ambiental. Como um importante centro logístico, Hai Phong está promovendo a redução do consumo de energia e das emissões provenientes do transporte, carga, descarga e armazenagem. A cidade está implementando com sucesso modelos de cultivo de arroz de baixa emissão em quase 3.964 hectares (de 2024 até o final da safra de 2025), contribuindo para a redução de mais de 19.101 toneladas de carbono equivalente, criando uma base para a formação de créditos de carbono. artigo.texto: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk says the company's best data center construction workers could be former baristas or shelf-stockers. "Those are some of our best people, and they've never done data centers before," Musk said earlier this week during a remote appearance at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin. Musk said that SpaceX has assembled an internal team, which he called "ArmyX," that has broken down all the jobs needed to construct data centers into smaller tasks "that are easily trainable in a few days." "You don't need people that have, say, been doing networking cables for their whole life," he said. "You divide the tasks into things that can be where you can train someone new who may have been a Starbucks barista or stocking shelves at Target." The billionaire praised the skills and work ethic that retail and fast-food workers could bring to data center construction. Musk specifically called attention to the skills of a former In-N-Out cook. "Let me tell you, if you get some aces out of In-N-Out who've been making epic burgers all day long perfectly, they're going to do a damn good job of network cables," he said. Musk says this team is powering SpaceX's expansion of its massive Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 data centers in Memphis. During SpaceX's most recent earnings call, Musk said that he "would be surprised" if the company added less than 13 gigawatts of compute by the end of 2027. Like the rest of the industry, SpaceX has a lot riding on the buildout. According to its latest earnings report, the company is spending more than ever on AI — and that could soon double. Business Insider previously reported that SpaceX offered employees a 20% pay increase if they volunteered to work six weeks in Memphis or Southaven, Mississippi, where another large data center is located. "These days when I go to Memphis, which I go to Memphis pretty frequently, it's becoming a well-oiled machine where it's just getting done," Musk said. "And we run a twenty-four-seven operation. So I can walk the site at one or two in the morning and see more or less the same productivity as I would the next morning at 10 AM, seven days a week."

artigo.texto: A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road. Moment Energy’s new Nova battery storage system puts those packs to work on commercial sites. And when a pack wears out, it can be swapped without pulling out the whole system. Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June. Each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power. It has a 2.94 m by 1.80 m (9.7 x 5.9 ft) footprint, and units can be linked together for projects in the tens of megawatt-hours. A site could charge the batteries when electricity is cheaper or when its solar panels are producing more than it needs, then draw on that power when demand spikes or the grid goes down. Nova can use packs from different EV models, even when those packs have aged at different rates. Moment’s battery management software tracks how each pack is doing. As packs wear out, the company can replace them while leaving the enclosure and concrete pad in place. Moment says its pack replacement service could keep a system in service for more than 20 years. “We see a future where reengineered EV batteries become essential infrastructure for powering businesses and onshoring manufacturing and supply chains. Nova brings that vision to life, combining safety, engineering, and North American manufacturing to deploy the safest and highest-performance batteries ever made: EV batteries to supercharge our aging grid,” said Edward Chiang, co-founder and CEO of Moment Energy. What the safety certifications mean Moment Energy says Nova is the first storage system built from retired EV batteries to earn both UL 1973 certification for the batteries and UL 9540 certification for the complete system. It was also tested under UL 9540A, which looks at how a battery fire can spread. The factory itself is certified under UL 1974, which covers how used batteries are assessed and graded for reuse. That matters for businesses with limited space. Nova is designed to sit outdoors alongside the buildings it serves. It uses liquid cooling, detects smoke, heat, and flammable gases, and is rated to operate from −13F to 122F (−25C to 50C). Moment Energy also says an independent review found that Nova meets US federal sourcing restrictions tied to the clean electricity investment tax credit. Those rules are one part of determining whether a project qualifies for the credit. Orders are open, and Moment Energy expects the first units to ship in Q1 2027 for deployments across North America. artigo.texto: ACME Solar Holdings Limited has announced the commissioning of additional battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity in Rajasthan through its wholly owned subsidiary, ACME Sigma Urja Private Limited. The company disclosed two commissioning milestones on November 20, 2026, covering projects located at Neemri village in Rawatbhata tehsil of Chittorgarh district, Rajasthan. Following these developments, the subsidiary has achieved a cumulative commissioned BESS discharge capacity of 175.72 MW / 733.939 MWh, with an installed capacity of 175.72 MW / 792.418 MWh. In its first regulatory filing submitted to BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India, ACME Solar reported that ACME Sigma Urja commissioned a discharge capacity of 35.81 MW / 148.645 MWh. The installed capacity of this commissioned portion stands at 35.81 MW / 160.48 MWh. This capacity forms part of a larger 50 MW / 209 MWh discharge capacity battery energy storage system, with an overall installed capacity of 50 MW / 220 MWh. The storage component is associated with the company’s TATA FDRE Power Project. ACME Solar clarified that only the battery energy storage system portion has been commissioned so far, while the commercial operation date (COD) is scheduled for November 22, 2026. The project is supported by a power purchase agreement (PPA) signed with The Tata Power Company Limited. In a separate regulatory disclosure, the company announced the commissioning of an additional 16.06 MW / 69.678 MWh of BESS discharge capacity at the same project location. The installed capacity of this additional portion stands at 16.06 MW / 75.225 MWh. This commissioning forms part of a larger 250 MW / 1,069 MWh discharge capacity firm and dispatchable renewable energy (FDRE) project, which has an overall installed capacity of 250 MW / 1,150 MWh. The company stated that this development follows an earlier intimation dated October 31, 2026. The commercial operation date for the newly commissioned capacity is also scheduled for November 22, 2026. With the latest additions, ACME Sigma Urja has strengthened its operational energy storage portfolio, taking its cumulative commissioned BESS discharge capacity to 175.72 MW / 733.939 MWh. The corresponding installed capacity has reached 175.72 MW / 792.418 MWh. Both disclosures were made under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. The regulatory filings were signed by Rajesh Sodhi, Company Secretary and Compliance Officer of ACME Solar Holdings Limited. The latest commissioning milestones reflect the company’s continued progress in developing grid-scale battery storage infrastructure alongside renewable energy projects in India. Battery energy storage systems are expected to play an important role in supporting renewable energy integration, improving power supply flexibility and enabling reliable electricity delivery during periods of changing generation and demand. artigo.texto: UK and EU Emissions Trading Scheme Link Welcomed for Cement Sector The UK and the EU have agreed to link their Emissions Trading Schemes, a move that the Mineral Products Association says carries implications for British cement producers. According to the Mineral Products Association, the arrangement was announced as part of the UK-EU reset deal at the Brussels summit on Friday, 20 November 2026. Martin Casey, senior director for cement and lime at the Mineral Products Association, described the linking as a positive development for UK cement makers, who would gain access to a larger and more stable carbon market. He indicated, however, that the measure does not resolve all outstanding issues and that the association will keep working with the government to create a level playing field for domestic manufacturers. Under the arrangement, carbon allowances can be used across both markets, and the link sets the stage for mutual exemptions from carbon border taxes. The association noted that the linking supports closer alignment between UK and EU carbon pricing, which it said should reduce the incentive for importers to send higher-carbon goods to the UK once the UK carbon border tax takes effect from January. Casey added that substantial work remains to narrow the gap between what domestic producers and importers pay for their emissions. For cement, he pointed to indirect cost compensation, changes to the CBAM rate method, and monitoring of import levels and other information as necessary to determine whether the carbon border rules are functioning as intended. artigo.texto: Quincy’s data center boom offers lessons for Montana communities QUINCY, Wash. — From the air, the contrast is clear: a growing agricultural town beside a sprawling data center hub. Quincy’s population has grown from about 5,000 to more than 8,000 over the past two decades, as the data center industry has expanded. The city is now home to eight data center campuses. For Montana Tech Lance Energy Chair Robert Morris, who serves on Montana’s Energy Task Force, Quincy’s growth offers a look at both the opportunities and challenges communities in Montana could face. “One thing we worry about is, are we going to be overwhelmed with the growth?” Morris said. “And they’ve stayed ahead of it here.” State Rep. Alex Ybarra, a lifelong Quincy resident, pointed to a new police station and City Hall and high school as examples of the public facilities built as the city changed thanks to an expanded tax base. Neighborhoods and businesses have also expanded. At the local school district, Superintendent Nik Bergman said data centers have become workforce partners. Bergman said the high school offers a data center technician program that can help students move directly into family-sustaining job within data centers. Quincy’s experience also raises questions facing Montana communities considering data center development: where facilities should be located, how much electricity and water will be needed, and who should pay for the infrastructure needed to support them? Ybarra said location matters because communities that host data centers can benefit from the tax revenue. He also said cities should be careful about the terms they accept. “If you do it wrong, like give away your water or whatever, ask for lower rates of electricity, then it doesn’t work,” Ybarra said. City data show Quincy’s eight data center campuses account for roughly 4% to 8% of the city’s total water use. Newer cooling technology is designed to operate without drawing additional water, but it requires more electricity. Grant County PUD reports residential electricity rates have risen 55% over the past 20 years, from 4.12 cents per kilowatt-hour in 2006 to 6.4 cents in 2026. The utility’s rate remains below the listed averages for Washington, Montana and the nation. The utility is planning major transmission upgrades to meet demand from additional data center development, along with another rate increase. On the question of infrastructure and who pays, Morris said Quincy’s data center companies paid for their own substations as they arrived, working with the community and Grant County PUD. “I think it’s important that the communities, the utility and the developers all work together,” Morris said. For Quincy, the transformation took two decades. Morris said the experience can offer Montana communities information as they weigh whether and how to pursue similar development.

artigo.texto: Ascendum Türkiye has partnered with global battery leader CATL to open Türkiye’s first NING Service Experience Center in Tuzla, Istanbul. Chinese battery giant CATL has signaled that it could make further investments in Türkiye after officially entering the country with the opening of its NING Service center in Istanbul. The facility, established in İstanbul in cooperation with Ascendum Türkiye with an investment of approximately 15 million euros, will provide services in a range of areas, from battery repair to the training of technical specialists. CATL Co-President of Sales and Marketing Bruce Li, who traveled to İstanbul for the opening, said the NING Service investment was the first step in the company’s long-term plans for Türkiye and signaled that CATL could consider larger investments in the country in the future. Commenting on the possibility of an electric vehicle battery investment in Türkiye, Li said: “As you know, one of the easiest options for us could be to find a local partner in Türkiye and work together on battery pack production. We can hold discussions.” “Battery cell production is a highly complex business. But yes, we are open to that as well. When the market grows and the conditions are right, we may also invest in battery cell production. If we find a suitable partner, we could also develop cooperation through licensing for cell production,” he added. Asked about CATL’s cooperation with Togg, Li said: “Togg is Türkiye’s domestic and largest electric vehicle manufacturer. We have advanced battery technologies. Therefore, what the two sides have, namely our technology and Togg’s needs, are aligned. We are working shoulder to shoulder to assess Türkiye’s electric vehicle market and the commercial opportunities in this field.”

artigo.texto: The National Wealth Fund has announced an equity investment in two battery energy storage projects in Eccles and Kilmarnock, Scotland, in partnership with Matrix Renewables UK Limited. As part of the partnership, Matrix will retain majority ownership of both projects, while the investment will support their development and implementation. Located along transmission corridors connecting Scotland and England, the projects will have a combined power capacity of 1 GW and an energy storage capacity of 2 GWh. Construction at the Eccles project is already underway, with commercial operations expected to commence in October 2027. Meanwhile, construction at the Kilmarnock project is scheduled to begin in December 2026, with commercial operations targeted for September 2028. Furthermore, once operational, the facilities are expected to provide storage capacity equivalent to the annual electricity consumption of approximately 520,000 households. In April 2026, Matrix Renewables secured £245 million in non-recourse financing for a 500 MW/1,000 MWh battery energy storage system project located in Eccles-Leitholm, Scotland. The project, being developed in partnership with EDF, commenced construction in November 2025. Commercial operations are expected to commence in the third quarter of 2027.

artigo.texto: Brasil disputa liderança na atração de data centers, diz The Economist CNN - O Brasil tenta aproveitar a expansão mundial da infraestrutura de inteligência artificial para se consolidar como um dos principais destinos de investimentos em data centers. O país aposta em oferta de energia renovável, mercado digital em crescimento e posição estratégica para conexões internacionais para atrair projetos. A movimentação já aparece em obras e anúncios de investimentos. Em Vinhedo, no interior de São Paulo, a Ascenty está ampliando um complexo de data centers e prevê novos empreendimentos. Segundo reportagem do The Economist, a empresa planeja investir US$ 1,2 bilhão na região, numa aposta no crescimento da demanda por capacidade computacional. A América Latina ainda tem participação pequena na infraestrutura global de processamento e armazenamento de dados. Segundo a revista, a região reúne menos de 600 data centers, com capacidade total próxima de 1,5 gigawatt (GW), volume inferior ao do Reino Unido. Já o Brasil, sozinho, concentra quase metade dessa capacidade: são aproximadamente 700 megawatts (MW) instalados — e a perspectiva é de crescimento. Alessandro Lombardi, presidente da Elea Data Centers, estima que a capacidade brasileira possa alcançar 5 GW até 2030. Energia e mercado consumidor atraem investimentos Um dos principais trunfos brasileiros é a matriz elétrica. Isso porque cerca de 85% da eletricidade do país vem de fontes renováveis. A disponibilidade de energia limpa é um diferencial, já que o setor demanda grandes volumes de eletricidade para se manter em funcionamento. O custo de construção também pode favorecer países latino-americanos. Um estudo da consultoria Turner & Townsend estima que erguer um data center no Vale do Silício custa cerca de US$ 14 por watt. Na América Latina, os valores variam de US$ 11,50 no México a US$ 9 em Bogotá, na Colômbia. Outro fator é o crescimento do consumo digital na região: quase 80% da população latino-americana já utiliza a internet, enquanto boa parte dos dados ainda é armazenado e processado nos Estados Unidos. Essa distância pode afetar a velocidade de acesso a serviços digitais: uma informação hospedada no estado americano da Virgínia pode levar cerca de 150 milissegundos para chegar a São Paulo. Quando o processamento ocorre em Vinhedo, o tempo cai para aproximadamente dois milissegundos. A redução da latência (intervalo entre o envio de uma solicitação e a resposta do sistema) é especialmente relevante para empresas que dependem de aplicações digitais rápidas. Isso cria uma demanda adicional por estruturas de processamento instaladas mais perto dos usuários. Brasil disputa projetos de inteligência artificial A oportunidade não se limita ao armazenamento de dados de usuários locais. Grandes empresas de tecnologia procuram regiões que possam funcionar como pontos estratégicos para suas redes globais de processamento. Um dos projetos mais expressivos nesse sentido é o da ByteDance, controladora do TikTok. A companhia chinesa planeja investir até US$ 39 bilhões em data centers no Complexo do Pecém, no Ceará. A vantagem do local é a proximidade com cabos submarinos que conectam a região à Europa, à África e a outros mercados. A disputa se estende às estruturas dedicadas ao treinamento de modelos de IA. Nesse caso, a prioridade é a disponibilidade de energia, custos e condições de operação, mais do que a proximidade com o mercado consumidor. David Dias, da consultoria EY, afirmou que a América Latina terá de disputar esses investimentos com regiões como Canadá, países nórdicos, Oriente Médio e Sudeste Asiático. O governo brasileiro também tenta estimular a chegada de empreendimentos através da redução de tarifas de importação sobre equipamentos de tecnologia, em uma iniciativa para tornar o país mais atrativo para investidores. Gargalos e disputa geopolítica podem frear expansão Apesar das vantagens, transformar o potencial em novos empreendimentos depende de superar obstáculos. A infraestrutura elétrica é um dos principais desafios: regiões com boa conexão à internet nem sempre são aquelas com maior disponibilidade de energia. Além disso, problemas na transmissão e a demora para obter autorização de conexão à rede podem comprometer o cronograma dos projetos. A segurança regulatória também pesa na decisão das empresas. Investidores querem previsibilidade em temas como incentivos fiscais e proteção à propriedade intelectual. Outro ponto é a aceitação da comunidade local. Embora a resistência a data centers seja menor na América Latina do que nos Estados Unidos, já existem registros de protestos contra esses projetos nas regiões visadas para as instalações. Para Fabro Steibel, do Instituto de Tecnologia e Sociedade do Rio de Janeiro (ITS-Rio), a questão geopolítica adiciona uma camada de complexidade. Na semana passada, o Departamento de Comércio dos Estados Unidos anunciou a exigência de licença para que data centers brasileiros recebam semicondutores avançados. A medida reflete a preocupação de Washington de que empresas chinesas possam utilizar, remotamente, equipamentos instalados em outros países para desenvolver modelos de inteligência artificial e contornar restrições americanas à exportação de chips.

artigo.texto: ANDERSON — As battery energy storage systems proliferate in the United States, officials have sought to dispel what they say are misconceptions about their safety. Battery energy storage systems, or BESS, help stabilize electrical grids by “providing steady power flow despite fluctuations from inconsistent generation of renewable energy sources and other disruptions,” according to the United States Environmental Protection Agency. The Clean Coalition, a nonprofit organization “whose mission is to accelerate the transition to renewable energy and a modern grid through technical, policy and project development expertise,” says BESS helps sources like solar panels and wind turbines reach their full potential by storing excess energy produced during times of high generation and dispersing it when those sources are unavailable. The facilities operate by using lithium-ion batteries to receive and store electrical currents, according to the Indiana Office of Energy Development. “Individual battery cells are grouped together to form battery packs,” according to a study commissioned by the IOED. “Each system has cooling and fire systems to manage safety risks. Each battery storage facility is required to provide emergency response plans as a condition of project approval through Indiana Department of Homeland Security. Operators are required to provide training to first responders, offering instruction on proper responses to battery storage system emergencies.” The Clean Coalition goes on to point out several benefits of BESS, including job creation and the generation of tax revenue for local governments. The Clean Coalition’s website also mentions that BESS is essential in reducing the “environmental footprint of energy generation,” and Rebecca TeKolste, the director of climate and energy at the Hoosier Environmental Council, said BESS is an important tool. “You’re really able to leverage those renewable resources throughout all times of the day, regardless of whether or not the wind is blowing and the sun is shining,” TeKolste said. “Batteries can store any kind of energy. It could be they’re storing energy from gas plants, solar — it really just depends on what the utility has in excess.” TeKolste acknowledged that some people hold safety concerns related to BESS, with several fires breaking out at facilities years ago. TeKolste said batteries are considerably safer now than they were in the past. “There’s always going to be some challenges with safety considerations,” TeKolste said. “Largely, those have been mitigated with the improvements of technology over the last couple of decades. I think now what we are seeing is the primary challenges with batteries rather than safety. Now they’re much more in the supply chain. “Batteries rely on rare Earth metals, and in some cases, there are some concerns about labor when it comes to where those metals are being mined.” Currently, there are nine operating utility-scale battery energy storage systems in Indiana. TeKolste said regulating them is difficult because decisions are typically made through local zoning ordinances. With 92 counties in Indiana, that means up to 92 different potential sets of rules. Sean Coffington, a clean energy organizer at Greenlight America, said that “battery energy storage systems, as part of the electrical grid, are a net environmental positive.” When talking about the placement of BESS facilities, Coffington said their installations near population clusters are logical. “You hear a lot about these systems being built near population centers,” Coffington said. “You can think of it like a water tower on top of an apartment building. We need electricity where the people are, and if we’re producing extra electricity, it makes sense to hold it in storage near where it will need to be used.” TeKolste said when looking at other alternatives, BESS is a better option. “If you look at an apples-to-apples comparison between mining, burning and storing coal ash, that is a known, certain risk to communities, whereas the battery technology has lower risk on almost every metric,” TeKolste said. “Everything has some level of risk, but the level of risk to a battery system is a lot lower than the level of risk of running a coal plant for the same amount of energy. “It’s all part of a system where there are trade-offs,” she continued. “From our perspective, batteries are a solution to get some of these more polluting, more expensive and more carbon-intensive resources offline faster and used significantly less.”

artigo.texto: Data centers se tornam alvos estratégicos de guerra Infraestrutura de computação é responsável pela comunicação e funcionamento em diversos serviços essenciais. Gerando resumo WASHINGTON — As empresas de tecnologia dos Estados Unidos estarão sujeitas a “um imposto enorme” se construírem centros de dados de inteligência artificial em outros países, afirmou nesta sexta-feira, 20, o presidente Donald Trump. Ele não deu detalhes e disse que ainda não havia informado seus próprios funcionários sobre a medida. O presidente republicano exortou os americanos a acolherem a construção de centros de dados em suas comunidades e a obterem concessões dos desenvolvedores, repetindo um argumento que apresentou antes das eleições de meio de mandato. “Vocês devem tirar proveito dos centros de dados”, disse Trump em uma entrevista à imprensa na Casa Branca. “Façam com que eles paguem a vocês, façam com que paguem à sua comunidade, mas não os impeçam de operar.” O Senado, liderado pelos republicanos, aprovou na quinta-feira, 19, uma legislação bipartidária que visa acelerar as análises de licenciamento para a construção de usinas de energia, linhas de transmissão e outras infraestruturas energéticas, à medida que os legisladores buscam aumentar o abastecimento energético do país para atender à crescente demanda e reduzir os preços da eletricidade. As mudanças abrangentes da legislação reduziriam o prazo para o início de grandes projetos de energia e garantiriam que os data centers paguem pela energia que consomem. A indignação em relação aos data centers e ao aumento dos preços da eletricidade ajudou a dar início a uma onda de democratas que se comprometeram a reprimir esses gigantes devoradores de energia. Espera-se que se siga um ambiente regulatório mais rigoroso para os gigantes da IA e os desenvolvedores de data centers, mesmo que Trump — talvez o maior defensor do setor — adie qualquer ação repressiva federal. Leia também - Como data centers se tornaram novos alvos estratégicos de guerra: ‘Brilham como árvores de Natal’ - Restrição de compra de chips pelo Brasil não inviabiliza data centers, mas atrapalha - Maiores data centers dos EUA já emitem tanto carbono quanto o de países inteiros Apesar do apoio de Trump, os data centers que alimentam o boom da inteligência artificial tornaram-se politicamente tóxicos. O setor de tecnologia afirma ter entendido a mensagem. Além de ampliar os incentivos financeiros, representantes do Google e da Meta disseram, em entrevistas à AP, que estão tentando combater a desconfiança por meio de maior transparência com as comunidades onde pretendem construir. As empresas também estão assumindo compromissos para reduzir seu impacto sobre o meio ambiente e oferecendo garantias de que os data centers elevarão o valor dos imóveis locais — tudo isso enquanto afirmam que a IA é uma força positiva para a economia americana, apesar dos céticos. Com as comunidades anfitriãs em todo o território dos EUA se voltando contra seus gigantescos data centers, os gigantes da tecnologia americana prometem receber menos recursos dos contribuintes, manter menos segredos ou injetar mais dinheiro nas comunidades dispostas a permitir a instalação desses centros de servidores. O governo Trump divulgou na segunda-feira novas regras para restringir o acesso remoto a chips e servidores avançados dos EUA, marcando o mais recente passo para limitar a capacidade da China de usar chips americanos para treinar seus melhores modelos de inteligência artificial. A medida atualiza as restrições às exportações de chips avançados para data centers de IA instalados no exterior, o que deve dificultar o acesso de empresas chinesas a tais componentes. As novas regras afetam o envio dos semicondutores para vários países, entre os quais o Brasil./AP

artigo.texto: Carteira permanece em desenvolvimento, não integra o plano de investimentos de R$ 21,1 bilhões para 2027 a 2030 e reúne diferentes configurações de armazenamento hidráulico, incluindo uma proposta reversível de 2,2 GW associada à hidrelétrica de Segredo. A Copel apresentou no Copel Day, realizado na quinta-feira (19), uma carteira de sete projetos de usinas hidrelétricas reversíveis no Paraná, ainda em desenvolvimento e sem contratação definida. A companhia pretende preparar os empreendimentos para futuras oportunidades de armazenamento de energia, condicionadas às regras dos leilões, ao licenciamento e às demais etapas regulatórias. A MegaWhat informou que os projetos somam cerca de 9 GW e têm diferentes configurações. Aproximadamente 6,6 GW correspondem a soluções de circuito semiaberto, que aproveitam um reservatório já existente e preveem outro para completar o sistema; a carteira inclui ainda projetos de circuito aberto e um empreendimento fechado de 200 MW. - Brasil reúne US$ 310 bilhões em 33 projetos de indústria limpa, mas só um alcançou decisão final de investimento em 12 meses - Exército Brasileiro contrata energia 100% renovável da Cemig para abastecer 160 unidades militares em nove estados e no Distrito Federal - China conecta à rede usina de 600 MWh que transforma ar em líquido a −194 °C para guardar energia solar e eólica e gerar por 10 horas - Neoenergia abre edital de R$ 60 milhões para financiar projetos de energia solar, baterias e modernização elétrica na Bahia Como funciona uma hidrelétrica reversível As usinas reversíveis funcionam com dois níveis de reservatórios. Em períodos de maior disponibilidade de eletricidade, a água é bombeada para o nível superior; quando há necessidade de geração, ela retorna pelo circuito hidráulico e movimenta as turbinas, permitindo deslocar o uso da energia entre horários diferentes. O bombeamento consome eletricidade e envolve perdas no processo, mas permite armazenar energia indiretamente por meio da água acumulada no reservatório superior. O mecanismo possibilita transferir seu uso entre períodos, inclusive diante da variação da geração de fontes como solar e eólica. Segundo as informações apresentadas pela companhia, os projetos podem oferecer entre 15 e 20 horas de armazenamento. Esse intervalo representa o período em que a energia acumulada na forma de água pode ser utilizada posteriormente, de acordo com a configuração de cada empreendimento e as condições de operação. A Copel trabalha com três configurações. Nos projetos de circuito aberto, os dois reservatórios permanecem ligados ao curso natural de um rio; no semiaberto, apenas um deles está conectado ao rio; no circuito fechado, os dois reservatórios ficam isolados dos cursos d’água. Segredo reúne projeto reversível de 2,2 GW Entre as propostas está uma usina reversível de 2,2 GW associada à hidrelétrica de Segredo. A MegaWhat registrou que esse é o projeto mais avançado da carteira e que o projeto básico foi submetido à Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) para aprovação. A iniciativa não deve ser confundida com a ampliação convencional de Segredo contratada no leilão de reserva de capacidade realizado em março deste ano. Essa expansão acrescentará 1,27 GW à usina e já está em construção, enquanto a reversível permanece em desenvolvimento e depende de contratação futura. A carteira também inclui dois projetos de circuito aberto, na modalidade pump back, em Foz do Areia e Segredo, além do projeto fechado de 200 MW. Nos empreendimentos semiabertos, a companhia pretende aproveitar reservatórios existentes, instalações e capacidade de escoamento já disponíveis. Diogo Mac Cord, vice-presidente de Estratégia, Novos Negócios e Transformação Digital da Copel, afirmou à MegaWhat que a variedade de configurações permite adaptar a participação da empresa ao desenho dos futuros certames. “Dependendo do tipo de leilão que o governo abrir, dependendo do volume, a gente consegue entrar com diferentes tipos de projeto”, disse. Carteira fica fora do plano de investimentos Os sete projetos reversíveis não fazem parte do plano de investimentos de R$ 21,1 bilhões previsto pela Copel para 2027 a 2030. O orçamento está direcionado a outros investimentos da companhia, e os empreendimentos de armazenamento, caso sejam viabilizados e contratados, exigirão recursos adicionais. Essa separação distingue projetos em desenvolvimento de obras já contratadas. A potência de cerca de 9 GW apresentada pela empresa não significa que todo esse volume será construído, porque cada empreendimento ainda precisa avançar em estudos, licenciamento, autorizações e definição do modelo de remuneração. A regulamentação também determinará em quais condições cada configuração poderá participar dos futuros processos de contratação. A Copel acompanha as discussões com a Aneel sobre os procedimentos para aprovação dos projetos e as definições do Ministério de Minas e Energia sobre o desenho dos certames. A Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE) abriu uma chamada para receber informações técnicas de Sistemas de Armazenamento Hidráulico, categoria que inclui as usinas reversíveis. O órgão informou que os dados serão usados em estudos de planejamento energético, formulação de políticas públicas e desenvolvimento de diretrizes e regras para futura contratação. A EPE esclareceu que a chamada não constitui procedimento de habilitação nem inscrição para uma contratação futura. O objetivo é conhecer iniciativas em diferentes níveis de maturidade e reunir informações sobre localização, características básicas e estágio de desenvolvimento, sem garantir participação posterior em processo competitivo. A Copel pretende manter os projetos em desenvolvimento enquanto acompanha a definição das regras e do formato dos próximos certames. A companhia estima que uma usina reversível possa demandar cerca de cinco anos de construção após a contratação, prazo que dependerá das características técnicas, ambientais e regulatórias de cada empre

artigo.texto: Elon Musk said AI companies may soon run into serious cash shortages as they wait for revenue-generating data centers to come online. The SpaceX and Tesla CEO replied to an X post on Saturday that showed comparatively low stock valuations for semiconductor manufacturers, relative to their expected profits. This could suggest that investors are bearish on AI-powering chip companies continuing to notch soaring profits in the race for compute — a sign that data center construction may face serious headwinds in the near future. "The cash shortage is also going to be nuts next year," Musk said, adding that delays in data center activations would require "hundreds of billions" in more capital for AI companies. "Where will that come from?" he asked. Tech stocks in US markets took it on the chin last week. The S&P 500 and the Dow entered correction territory on Friday, meaning they had fallen at least 10% from recent highs. The market carnage prompted some to speculate that the AI bubble had popped. Financial regulators in semiconductor-heavy Taiwan on Saturday said they would limit short selling — an action similar to one taken by US regulators during the 2008 housing crisis. Though leading AI and AI-adjacent companies like Meta, Microsoft, and Anthropic are reporting growing revenue, they're also spending massive sums to secure compute — powered by key hardware that enables chatbots and other AI tools. Compute is largely provided by data centers, which have faced their own series of setbacks recently, from backlash from the communities where they are being built to the blue midterm wave and construction delays. And without a reliable network of data centers, AI companies are hobbled in their ability to scale to meet investor demand. Data center operators, meanwhile, are left at the altar with their multibillion-dollar investments failing to generate revenue. "Getting this amount of compute turned on, cooled and working reliably is incredibly hard," Musk said.
